summary: Five independent agenda designs from different lenses, then three critical judges score and cross-examine them
logs: designs returned: policy-repair, advantage-theory, experimentalist-task, evaluation-statistics, paper-strategy

agenda.thesis: If results are positive, the paper claims that the constant-action collapse of SCM-conditioned LLM intervention policies was an engineering failure, not a limit of small language models: the supervision, the training exposure, the state interface and the action interface were all broken. Forward-only forensics and an interventional factorial show directly that the deployed adapters never read the posterior, and a gate suite fixed in advance catches the collapse from files the training job wrote. With one high-precision planner teacher, listwise soft targets, permuted single-token actions, a compact state that is sufficient for the planner, adequate data and on-policy relabeling, Qwen3-0.6B recovers planner-quality decisions on held-out systems (closed-loop relative regret at most 0.15, design quality within 5% of target-risk planning). It matches a numerical student trained on identical data and passes counterfactual tests of posterior sensitivity. Having earned that, the policy, or a hybrid in which the LLM supplies the planner's prior, is tested on fresh systems in a world class chosen by headroom criteria that use no LLM output; an advantage there at lower experimental cost would meet the submission condition. If results are null or negative, the paper becomes a controlled diagnostic. It shows with direct evidence why the collapse happened, and that numerical students learn the planner's state-to-action mapping that the LLM cannot learn, or can learn only when handed planner statistics, which is narration. The LLM's claimed role then narrows to supplying priors to a numerical planner, or the paper reports a bounded negative result with validated gates. In no branch does a negative result trigger a replacement benchmark; any class change follows only the headroom rule fixed in advance.

experiments.name: Reference targets and supervision-quality audit
experiments.question: What should a learned policy imitate, how precise must that target be, and how much could the old four-teacher supervision have taught even if fitted perfectly?
experiments.decision_rule:
Training proceeds only if the precision gate passes at D <= 16,384 and the rounding criterion passes at 3 digits. If rounding fails, the compact interface keeps 4 digits; that choice is made here without any LLM.
Old-supervision ceiling regret >= 0.30: the paper may state that the old label process could not have taught planner-quality decisions even with infinite data. Ceiling <= 0.15: the label process was adequate in the limit, and the binding defects were volume, exposure and interface.
Positive: a precise teacher that costs no environment responses, which justifies dropping measured-preference DPO in this class.
Null (irreducible multi-way ties): report the tie fraction and use near-tie-tolerant agreement everywhere.
Negative (CRN planner disagrees with the saved receipts): stop and fix before any training.
experiments.prerequisites: Local CPU only. Needs a reviewed in-repository CRN planner; the scratch re-implementations are not in project custody. The truth-conditional option needs lead approval to use private training-world descriptors.
experiments.cost: About 20 CPU-minutes in total. Basis: 0.119 s per state at 16,384 draws (a vectorised re-implementation scored 4,203 states in 499 s on this Mac, verifier log v09.log). About 300 lines of code; 1-2 days calendar. Zero GPU, zero CURC.
experiments.main_risk: The teacher is a myopic working-model planner that is suboptimal under the shifted prior, so planner quality is measured against an imperfect teacher. Acceptable in this class because Finding A bounds any policy's edge over it at a few percent.

experiments.name: Forward-only forensics of the deployed policies: score tables, decoding audit, counterfactual sensitivity, probes and retrospective gates
experiments.question: Did the constant action come from a base-model prior, supervised training, DPO drift or the decoder? Does any checkpoint respond to the SCM posterior, and does its hidden state encode it?
experiments.decision_rule:
Predeclared:
- D1, decoding contributed: whole-command argmax changes >= 10% of SFT deployment decisions.
- D2, base prior contributed: the base model puts >= 0.5 of its set-subtree mass on set_x_neg on training prompts.
- D3, posterior-blind: the CSC 95% upper bound is < 0.1 for SFT and final, while spurious sensitivity to budget, history or menu order is >= 0.10.
- D4, representation present: probe increment >= 0.10 with lower bound > 0. Absent: upper bound < 0.05.
- D5, gate validity: G2-G4 fail SFT and DPO and pass target risk and local information.
Positive (D3 and D5): the paper states with direct evidence that the deployed adapters did not read the posterior and that the collapse was detectable from training-time files.
Null (CSC interval spans 0.1-0.3): posterior use is undetermined; rely on E3's interventional attribution.
Negative (CSC >= 0.3 for SFT): the adapters read the posterior, but a command prior and the decoder dominated. Reframe the diagnosis as prior domination.
D4 absent points to a representation bottleneck and supports the compact interface. D4 present points to a knowing-doing gap, supports readout fixes and enables the hidden-state action head in E7.
experiments.prerequisites: Lead approval of local forward-only inference under a written protocol (local torch and transformers differ from the frozen runtime), or a CURC GPU ceiling of about 2 slice-hours. E1's planner. New code: a reviewed scoring harness with prefix-shared scoring and hidden-state capture, plus an edit generator (about 500 lines).
experiments.cost:
About 16,400 forwards (5,574 for the tables plus 10,800 for the battery) on 2-4k-token prompts, plus about 700 short probe forwards.
- Mac: 1.4-6.8 h at an assumed 0.3-1.5 s per forward. This is unmeasured; a 20-prompt pilot fixes it.
- CURC: 0.55-1.8 GPU-slice-hours at the ledger's 0.12-0.4 s per forward. The upper end exceeds the 0.76 h remainder.
Planner rescoring of 3,600 edited states takes about 7 CPU-minutes. 3-5 days including the protocol.
experiments.main_risk: Local numerics may not reproduce near-tie decisions; the fidelity gate guards against this. Posterior swaps produce internally inconsistent envelopes that are out of distribution for every checkpoint; the C3 edits partly control for this.

experiments.name: Collapse attribution factorial on the original 128 training states
experiments.question: Holding the training states fixed, which single repair (labels, state and action interface, or exposure) removes the constant action, for the LLM and for the numerical student?
experiments.design:
States: the exact 128 nonterminal snapshot states the deployed models were trained on. No new responses.
2 x 2 x 2 factorial:
- Labels: S0, the original mixed four-teacher hard labels, or S2, the planner soft targets from E1.
- Interface: original (string ids, fixed menu order, full-precision JSON with raw history, trie-greedy decoding, whole-command loss) or repaired (per-example random assignment of the single-token codes A-H, verified as single tokens with ids 32-39; random menu order; compact text sufficient for the planner; argmax over legal codes).
- Exposure: single pass at batch 1 (seed 1 in the original roster order, seed 2 in random order) or converged (10 shuffled epochs, batch 16, cosine lr 1e-4).
LLM runs: capacity is held at the deployed LoRA rank 8 on q/v, so it is not confounded. 16 runs.
Numerical student: the original 8,891-wide ranker MLP versus a repaired permutation-equivariant per-action posterior network, with the same label and exposure factors and 3 seeds. 24 CPU runs.
Anchor checks:
- the S0 / original / single-pass / roster cell should reproduce >= 75% of one action on the 128 states (saved: 108/128);
- the numerical anchor should reproduce the saved ranker pattern (>= 90% of score variance from action identity).
Controls: state-shuffled labels within graph x cost cells in the all-repaired cell; the constant plurality baseline; the coarse baseline N0.
Evaluation sets (about 1,340 states per run):
- the 128 training states, in-sample;
- the other 569 saved decision states of the same 32 worlds;
- 32 new validation worlds x 24 states from the E4 corpus.
Endpoints: maximum action share (collapse means >= 0.75), near-tie-tolerant agreement (chosen action within 5% relative regret of the best), mean relative regret, and interaction share of the score table.
experiments.decision_rule:
A factor is a sufficient repair if fixing it alone drops the max share below 0.6 and raises near-tie-tolerant agreement by >= 0.15 over the constant baseline, in both seeds. It is necessary if reverting it in the all-repaired cell restores collapse.
An order effect is confirmed if the single-pass roster order collapses and the single-pass random order does not.
The state-shuffled control must stay at or below N0. If it matches the real labels, learning is coarse-feature only.
Positive: interventional attribution of the observed collapse on identical states. The paper can say which defect was sufficient.
Null (collapse or N0-level regret in every cell): 128 states cannot teach state dependence under any repair. The paper states the collapse was overdetermined by data volume, and the scale-up in E4/E5 becomes the test.
Negative (the anchor does not collapse): the collapse is fragile to runtime or order, which narrows every diagnostic claim. Reconcile with the saved logs before interpreting further.
experiments.prerequisites:
E1 targets and the E2 fidelity result.
A new reviewed training engine (about 800-1,200 lines, reused through E9): soft targets over codes or whole commands, minibatches, scheduler, all-linear LoRA option, gate computation.
A GPU ceiling, or approval for local LoRA training.
A lead ruling that the single-pass cells are not a rerun of the old pipeline (they use a new engine, no DPO and no environment responses).
experiments.cost:
LLM: original-interface cells use 2-4k-token prompts at about 0.3-0.6 s per step; repaired cells use about 600 tokens at 0.05-0.2 s per step. These rates are an assumption scaled from the saved 0.62 s batch-1 SFT update. Training about 1 h, evaluation about 11k forwards at 0.5-1.5 h, total about 1.5-3 GPU-slice-hours.
Numerical: CPU minutes.
4-6 days calendar, mostly building the engine.
experiments.main_risk: With only 128 states every cell may fail out of world, so the attribution would hold only in-sample. The original-interface LLM cells are expensive per step.

experiments.name: Numerical learnability ladder (data volume x representation x target)
experiments.question: Can any numerical learner recover planner-quality decisions from the public SCM state of held-out systems, and with how much data, which representation and which target?
experiments.decision_rule:
Planner-quality acceptance:
- PQ-weak: closed-loop regret <= 0.15 (local information 0.154, coverage 0.441); 95% upper bound of the geometric-mean J/J_TR <= 1.05 (local information x1.02, leave-one-out public static schedule x1.208, coverage x1.35); and regret <= N0 - 0.10 with the CI excluding 0.
- PQ-strong: regret <= 0.08 and J/J_TR <= 1.02.
N* is the smallest N at which N1 or N2 passes PQ-weak.
Positive: planner-quality decisions are learnable from the public state. The paper says the earlier collapse was a supervision and exposure failure, not an impossibility. The LLM gets N_LLM = min(max(N*, 128), 512) worlds and the representation level that passed.
Null (only N3 passes): the LLM interface must carry the same derived summaries, and the LLM claim narrows to reading an SCM summary.
Negative (nothing passes at 2,048 worlds, or nothing beats N0 by 0.10): abandon the direct-policy route in this class (A1) and move the LLM to the hybrid role.
If N0 itself passes PQ-weak, the class does not discriminate posterior use, and only counterfactual tests can show posterior reading.
experiments.prerequisites:
E1 teacher.
Lead approval to generate a training-scope synthetic corpus with new world IDs (no development or confirmation IDs).
New code, about 1,000 lines: a learnability protocol module; an in-process rollout harness (the existing per-decision subprocess design costs about 48 s per episode), checked to reproduce saved training trajectories exactly; the equivariant student; evaluation.
experiments.cost: Labelling about 166k states x 0.119 s = 5.5 CPU-hours at 16,384 draws (about 1.4 h at 4,096), parallel across Mac cores. 168 small model fits: 3-10 CPU-hours. Closed-loop evaluation: 1-2 CPU-hours. Zero GPU, zero CURC. 5-7 days calendar.
experiments.main_risk: Finding A says reading the state is worth only 10-20% of final expected NMSE over a good graph-and-menu schedule, so N0 may approach the planner and the ladder may discriminate only weakly. The corpus generator is a second implementation of the protocol and must match saved trajectories.

experiments.name: LLM listwise distillation with the repaired interface, gates and leave-one-fix-out ablations
experiments.question: Given the data volume and representation at which a numerical student succeeded, can Qwen3-0.6B learn a state-dependent, planner-quality intervention policy from the SCM state in text, and which repairs are necessary?
experiments.design:
Data: the E4 corpus at N_LLM worlds x 24 states per world, sampled across all trajectory types (12.3k states at the 512-world cap). E4's validation and test worlds.
A-full recipe:
- State text: compact and sufficient for the planner. Posterior means, SDs and correlations rounded per E1; costs; budget; task; history summarized as per-action counts and the last three actions.
- Actions: per-example random menu order and random assignment of the single-token codes A-H.
- No stop action. Planners never stop in this class, so budget exhaustion ends the episode.
- Loss: soft-target cross-entropy over the eight legal code tokens, renormalized.
- Decoding: argmax with a keyed random tie-break.
- Capacity: LoRA rank 16, alpha 32 on all seven linear projections (10.1M parameters versus 1.15M before), matching Kriz et al.'s main configuration.
- Optimization: AdamW with lr from {5e-5, 2e-4} chosen on validation regret using 128 worlds; cosine schedule; 3% warmup; effective batch 32; 2 epochs; shuffled minibatches stratified by graph x cost x budget bin; clip 1.0, with lr halved if > 50% of steps are clipped; early stopping on validation regret.
Stage 1:
- A-full x 3 seeds;
- label-permuted control (targets from another state in the same graph x cost x budget cell) x 1 seed;
- the frozen base model, zero-shot, with the new interface;
- N2, N1 and N0 retrained on the identical states.
Stage 2, only if Stage 1 passes the gates: leave-one-fix-out ablations, 1 seed each (a second seed if the effect is < 2x the Stage-1 seed SD):
- -codes: original string ids, fixed order, trie-greedy, listwise loss over whole-command log-probs;
- -compact: original full-precision JSON with raw history, compared at matched steps;
- -soft: hard labels;
- -capacity: rank 8 on q/v;
- -volume: 32 worlds. Paired with N2 at 32 worlds, this also measures a pretraining sample-efficiency effect.
Gates on validation worlds, before any test scoring:
- G1: legality 100%.
- G2: max action share <= max(0.6, reference-optimal share + 0.15), and chosen-action entropy >= 0.5 x the reference's.
- G3: near-tie-tolerant agreement >= N0 + 0.15.
- G4: held-out soft-target CE <= the state-blind frequency model - 0.20 nats.
- G5: CSC >= 0.3 (lower bound > 0.1) on posterior swaps, and total variation <= 0.10 on invariant edits.
- G6: state x action interaction share >= 0.5 x the reference's.
- G7: across 3 seeds, SD of validation regret <= 0.03 and action-histogram total variation <= 0.15.
- G8: closed loop on 64 validation worlds, regret <= 0.20 and longest repeated-action run <= the planner's 99th percentile + 3.
Monitoring every 500 steps aborts the run if any action exceeds 60% on three consecutive checks.
Sample size: about 12k states (Qiu et al. used 6,240 examples, Paprika 17,181 trajectories); 3 seeds, the minimum to estimate seed spread; 256 test worlds as in E4.
Endpoints: closed-loop test-world regret, J/J_TR, parity with N2, gate profile, ablation deltas.
experiments.decision_rule:
Pass = G1-G8 + PQ-weak + parity (|regret_LLM - regret_N2| <= 0.05 at equal data).
Positive: the paper's mechanism claim, that a small LLM reads an explicit SCM posterior and chooses planner-quality interventions on held-out systems, with leave-one-fix-out attribution. This meets submission requirement 1 for this class. It is not an advantage, because the planner is the ceiling here.
Null (G1-G4 pass but G5 fails, or regret is 0.15-0.30): the LLM learned a coarse schedule; go to E7.
Negative (G2-G4 fail while N2 passes): the language interface is the bottleneck; go to E7, and if E7 fails, abandon the direct route (A2).
A pass obtained only with per-action planner statistics in the prompt is narration and does not count.
If the LLM beats N2 at 32 worlds by >= 0.05 regret, report a pretraining sample-efficiency effect, not an advantage.
experiments.prerequisites:
E3 engine, E4 corpus and N*, E1 targets.
A lead-approved GPU ceiling (about 4-17 slice-hours) or approval for local LoRA training on the Mac.
Runs longer than about 45 min need a longer-wall QoS or the Mac, because gpu-testing caps jobs at 1 h and resumed optimization across jobs is unqualified.
experiments.cost:
One A-full run = 512 x 24 x 2 = 24.6k example-steps at an assumed 0.05-0.2 s per step, so 0.34-1.4 h per run. Basis: the saved SFT update took 0.62 s at batch 1 on 2-4k-token prompts with strict determinism and checkpointing; compact prompts are about 600 tokens and minibatched. A pilot fixes the rate.
- Stage 1: about 1.6-6 h.
- Stage 2: about 2-8 h (-compact uses about 5x longer prompts at half the steps).
- Evaluation: about 110k single-forward decisions, 0.6-3 h.
Total about 4-17 GPU-slice-hours; assumed 2-4x longer on the Mac. 6-9 days calendar.
experiments.main_risk: A 0.6B model may not read rounded numeric posteriors from text well enough, and LoRA results may vary across seeds at this data scale. Critics may say the compact interface makes the task easier; the -compact ablation and E1's sufficiency argument, which does not depend on the LLM, answer that.

experiments.name: Closed-loop on-policy correction (DAgger with planner relabeling)
experiments.question: Does the trained policy remain planner-quality on its own state distribution, and does on-policy relabeling remove compounding error?
experiments.design:
Triggered if E5 passes at state level but closed-loop regret > 0.15 or G8 fails; otherwise run one confirmatory round.
Three DAgger rounds. Each round:
- rolls the current policy out in 256 fresh training-scope worlds, with planner-action mixing beta = 0.5, 0.25, 0;
- relabels every visited state with the reference planner (labels cost no environment responses; synthetic rollout responses are counted in the training ledger);
- aggregates the data and fine-tunes for one epoch.
Alternative loss arm on the same on-policy states: the exact expected-score objective -sum_a pi(a|s) s(a|s) + entropy 0.01. With a single-token action and known planner scores the policy-gradient expectation is exact, so GRPO-style sampling would add variance and no information.
Controls: the E5 checkpoint without on-policy data; N2 with identical DAgger rounds.
Sample size: about 6k new states per round (about 50% of the base corpus); tested on E4's 256 test worlds.
Endpoints: closed-loop test regret, J/J_TR, stress-state regret, longest repeated-action run.
experiments.decision_rule:
Adopt the smallest on-policy procedure that passes PQ-weak and G8 on the test worlds.
Positive: on-policy relabeling is reported as necessary, or as unnecessary if round 0 already passes.
Negative (both arms fail while the state-level gates pass): closed-loop failure (A3). The claim narrows to state-level imitation, and the LLM arm becomes the hybrid.
experiments.prerequisites: E5 state-level pass; the E4 rollout harness with LLM-in-the-loop forward passes.
experiments.cost: Rollouts: 3 x 256 x 24 = 18.4k forwards (0.1-0.4 h). Relabeling: 18.4k states x 0.119 s = 0.6 CPU-hours. Fine-tuning: 1-5 h. Total 1.5-6 GPU-slice-hours; 3-4 days.
experiments.main_risk: Aggregation may over-weight unusual on-policy states and degrade performance on the primary distribution; three rounds may be too few.

experiments.name: Capacity and interface escalation, and the direct-versus-hybrid decision
experiments.question: If the repaired 0.6B direct policy fails where the numerical student succeeds, does a predeclared escalation fix it, or should the language model move to a hybrid role?
experiments.decision_rule:
The first escalation that passes E5's full criteria becomes the frozen configuration, and the paper reports the minimum capacity or representation needed. Arm (c) must be described as an LLM encoder plus a linear action head.
Abandon the direct-policy route if any of these holds:
- A1: no numerical student passed in E4;
- A2: no arm in (a)-(d) passes while N2 passes, or the LLM passes only with per-action planner statistics;
- A3: the state-level gates pass but closed loop fails after E6.
Also make the hybrid primary if A4 holds in E8 (headroom concentrated in prior information: H2 >= 1.15 with H1 < 1.05 and H3 < 1.03).
A negative outcome licenses a documented direct-policy failure, with numerical students as positive controls. The LLM arm in E9-E10 is then H-prior.
experiments.prerequisites: E5 and E6 outcomes; approval for the Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct weights; the same engine.
experiments.cost: (a)-(c): 0.4-2 GPU-slice-hours each. (d): 1-5 h (about 2.5x the parameters). Total 3-12 GPU-slice-hours; 3-6 days.
experiments.main_risk: Escalation could turn into an open-ended search with many forking paths. The fixed order, one seed per arm and a single confirmation rule control this.

experiments.name: LLM-independent headroom audit to select the advantage class
experiments.question: In which candidate world class could any policy beat target-risk planning by a resolvable margin, and is the planner's decision mapping learnable there, judged without running any language model?
experiments.design:
Runs in parallel from week 1, CPU only.
Candidate classes that need only small or medium code changes:
(i) partial measurement with large cost ratios on 4-6 nodes;
(ii) informed priors from prose, with 0-2 initial observations and varied text;
(iii) wrong-known or unknown noise;
(iv) graph uncertainty, only if (i)-(iii) fail (a large change).
Per class: 64 synthetic training-scope systems, run with numerical policies only: target risk, plan-once static design, best public static schedule, a rollout (non-myopic) planner, an oracle-prior planner with the generating prior encoded numerically, an uninformed planner, and the N2 student ladder.
Criteria:
- H1, adaptivity: J(plan-once)/J(sequential) >= 1.10.
- H2, information headroom: J(uninformed)/J(oracle prior) >= 1.15.
- H3, non-myopic headroom: J(target risk)/J(rollout) >= 1.05.
- H4, resolvability: <= 150 systems for 80% power on a 10% difference on the class's primary endpoint, with common random numbers.
- H5, learnability: N2 reaches PQ-weak with <= 2,048 worlds.
Sample-size basis: with 64 systems, a 10% J difference has z of 4.5 at SD 0.171 and 22 at SD 0.035; a 5% difference has z of 2.3 and 11.
experiments.decision_rule:
Selection rule, fixed now: among classes passing H4 and H5, choose the largest H2 if the hypothesized LLM contribution is semantic; otherwise choose the largest max(H1, H3). Ties go to the lower code cost. No LLM output is used, which satisfies the standing rule on benchmark changes.
If no class passes, the paper reports that no tested class offers resolvable headroom, and E9-E10 are not run (a negative or diagnostic paper).
If the selected class satisfies A4, the hybrid is the primary LLM arm.
experiments.prerequisites: Lead approval of the selection rule now, and of the protocol code for each class. A pip install of causalchamber only if class (ii) uses its simulators.
experiments.cost: CPU only: about 1-4 CPU-hours per class for the rollout planner, plus E4-scale student fits. Code: 2-5 days per small or medium class. 1-3 weeks calendar for (i)-(iii).
experiments.main_risk: The class with the most headroom may be the costliest to code before venue deadlines. The thresholds are judgement calls, fixed in advance.

experiments.name: Privileged-teacher training, gates and ablation arms in the selected class
experiments.question: Does the frozen recipe transfer to the selected class, and do the arms needed to separate language pretraining, ACE-specific training, causal structure and extra computation pass the same gates?
experiments.decision_rule:
Only arms that pass G1-G8 enter E10. The LLM arm also needs PQ-weak relative to the privileged teacher on validation worlds.
If neither the direct nor the hybrid LLM arm passes, there is no advantage test, and the paper reports transfer failure.
If the text-ablated LLM equals the full LLM on validation, the semantic-contribution hypothesis is already falsified, and E10 is framed as a test of amortized planning only.
experiments.prerequisites: E8 selection; the frozen E5-E7 recipe; a GPU ceiling; protocol code for the selected class.
experiments.cost: About 3-10 GPU-slice-hours for the LLM arms plus 3-10 for the ablation arms. Numerical arms on CPU. 2-3 weeks.
experiments.main_risk: The privileged teacher may be out of reach from public information. The oracle prior may leak into the text if the text generator is not separated from the parameter draw.

experiments.name: Preregistered fresh-system advantage test
experiments.question: On fresh systems, does the language-model arm (direct or hybrid) reach a reliable answer at lower experimental cost than strong numerical policies given the same information?
experiments.design:
Preregistered before any system is generated.
Arms, all frozen from E9: the LLM arm, the hybrid, target risk with the same information, the rollout planner, the N2 student, the frozen LLM, the coarse baseline N0, and the ablation arms.
Fresh system IDs. Common random numbers across arms, which requires lifting the per-arm measurement-namespace rule at paired_episode.py:114-117; otherwise, replicate episodes per system.
A shared public stop rule.
Primary endpoint and n come from E8's H4 power analysis (<= 150 systems). Decision-level regret and realized error are secondaries.
Censoring and failure treatment are fixed in the preregistration.
experiments.decision_rule:
The LLM arm must be superior to target risk with the same information on the primary endpoint at one-sided alpha 0.05, with Holm correction across the predeclared contrasts. The hybrid is tested for non-inferiority against its own planner, with the margin fixed in the preregistration.
Positive: submission condition 2 is met for this class.
Null: a bounded negative, reported with its interval.
Negative: narrow the claim. No replacement benchmark.
experiments.prerequisites: E9 freeze; custody redesign for >= 100 systems (sharded archives); a compute ceiling.
experiments.cost: Per the ledger, 100-150 systems need about 22-35 CPU core-hours and 1.9-2.9 GPU slice-hours under the old per-decision process model. The LLM arms add about 21.6k decisions. 6-10 days calendar.
experiments.main_risk: The endpoint may be underpowered or censored, and failure modes may appear only on fresh systems.

- Then E9, preregistration and E10.
- E8 runs alongside E4-E7, and the E3 numerical runs alongside E4.

Venue fit: ICML 2027 (abstract January 14, paper January 22) realistically holds E1-E6, a diagnostic plus learnability paper. E8-E10 more plausibly target UAI 2027, NeurIPS 2027 or TMLR.

- E3: 1.5-3 h.
- E5-E7: 8.5-35 h, with hard stops at the gates. E5 Stage 1 is the only commitment before Gate C.

Local torch and transformers differ from the frozen runtime, so a gate requiring >= 99% reproduction of the saved decisions applies. Alternative: grant about 2 GPU-slice-hours on CURC for E2.

Approve generating a training-scope synthetic learnability corpus with new world IDs only, and planner relabeling on local CPU (E1, E4, E6). Synthetic responses would be reported as training cost; no development or confirmation IDs are touched.

Set a staged GPU ceiling (E3 about 3 h; E5-E7 up to about 35 h, with hard stops at the predeclared gates), or approve local LoRA training on the Mac. Also approve a QoS with more than a 1 h wall, or a full A100: gpu-testing caps jobs at 1 h and resumed optimization across jobs is unqualified.

Approve the new reviewed training-engine version (listwise soft targets, minibatching, scheduler, all-linear LoRA). Make the behavioural gate suite G1-G8 mandatory acceptance for every trained policy, replacing the legality-only gate.

Approve redirecting feedback in the known-graph class away from measured 4-replicate preferences and DPO, to planner relabeling plus on-policy (DAgger) relabeling. This is a method redirect justified by the label-noise evidence.
Conditionally approve Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (already in the local cache) as E7 escalation step (d), and rule now whether Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is ever in scope.

Approve the E8 class-selection rule now, before any LLM result exists in a new class, and the protocol code for up to three candidate classes. Approve the causalchamber pip install only if class (ii) uses its simulators.
Optional: approve the truth-conditional label analysis using the 32 private training-world descriptors (E1).
Rule whether E3's single-pass cells count as rerunning the old pipeline. They use a new engine, no DPO and no environment responses.
Set the venue and date, and say whether a diagnostic-plus-learnability paper is acceptable if E8-E10 cannot finish or come out negative.
what_not_to_do: Do not collect more 4-replicate measured preferences or scale DPO in the known-graph class. About 70% of strict labels are at noise level, carrying about 0.107 bits each, and collection consumed 90% of collection units.
Do not select recipes, temperatures, gate thresholds or interfaces on the 24 development systems. Their prompts serve E2 forensics only.
Do not put per-action planner statistics in the LLM prompt as a candidate arm. That is narration. Keep them as an upper-bound control, reported alongside an argmax-of-prompt baseline.
Do not keep greedy token-by-token trie decoding over multi-token commands, a fixed menu order, fixed identifiers or alphabetical tie-breaks.
Do not deploy or roll out any checkpoint that has not passed G1-G8, and never train with a single unshuffled pass at batch size 1.
Do not add hand-coded caps, diversity fills, collapse breakers or fallbacks. Every executed action must be model-chosen.
Do not present the old exposure-matched ranker as the learned numerical control. Use the converged N1 and N2 students trained on identical data.
Do not claim an advantage in the three-node known-graph class. Regret measured against the planner cannot show one, and Finding A bounds the room at a few percent.
Do not use first-crossing cost on 24 systems as an endpoint for learnability.
Do not escalate model size before the repaired 0.6B recipe has been gated, and never outside the predeclared E7 order.
Do not change world class because the LLM failed. A class is selected only by the E8 rule, which uses no LLM output.
Do not rerun the 24-system screen or the old collection, training or campaign pipelines.
Do not keep stop as a policy action in this class. Stop labels existed only at forced terminal states and produced the early-stop artifact; use a shared public stop rule if stopping matters.
biggest_uncertainties: Whether a 0.6B model can read rounded numeric posteriors from text well enough to act on them. E2's probes and E5 settle this; the literature on number handling is pessimistic.

Whether the three-node class has enough posterior-driven state dependence beyond coarse features for the learnability ladder to discriminate. Finding A says reading the state is worth only 10-20% of final expected NMSE, so the coarse baseline N0 may come close to the planner.
The speed and numerical fidelity of local MPS execution, and the true per-step LoRA training cost with compact prompts. Both are unmeasured, so every GPU figure here is a range pending a pilot.

Whether any class with resolvable headroom can be coded before the venue deadlines, and whether the LLM's contribution there would enter through the action (direct policy) or through the model (hybrid prior).
Whether the privileged or myopic teacher in the selected class is a good enough distillation target. If not, learning from realized outcomes would be required, and that signal is noisy.
Seed variance of LoRA training at about 10k states, and whether the training-cost accounting can be reconciled with any savings at deployment.
theory_items: Belief-state sufficiency. In the known-graph linear-Gaussian known-noise class, both the target-risk score and the Bayes-optimal sequential policy depend on the history only through the conjugate posterior (plus costs, budget and task). This justifies a compact interface without reference to LLM performance, and it makes history edits a clean test of spurious dependence.

Trie-greedy versus whole-command argmax. Greedy decoding picks the branch with the largest subtree mass M(b) = sum over its commands of p(c), not the most likely command. Characterize the region where observe_all is the argmax command yet loses because p(observe) < M(set), and show that single-token codes make greedy decoding equal to argmax.

State-blind collapse lemma. A model whose output ignores state minimizes listwise cross-entropy at the average target p-bar, so argmax decoding yields a constant action. With token-factorized logits and suffix tokens shared between X and Y, that argmax follows per-node pluralities, which explains set_x_neg from the pooled _neg counts (32+10 versus 29+10). This formalizes the 8-logit model of the DPO pass.

Label-information bound. The 4-replicate, 2-SE tie rule has alpha = P(|t3| > 2) = 0.139, and a 31% flip rate leaves 1 - H2(0.31) = 0.107 bits per strict label. Contrast this with planner labels, whose flip probability is Phi(-gap/sigma_D) outside a declared tie band, and derive the number of draws D needed for at most 1% flips.

Exact on-policy gradient for single-step known rewards. For a single-token action with known per-action scores, the gradient of E_pi[s] equals sum_a s(a) grad pi(a), so GRPO-style sampling adds variance and no information. Combined with DAgger's no-regret guarantee, this shows that in this class only the on-policy state distribution matters.

Regret-to-design-quality bridge. Under local additivity of one-step risk reductions, which holds approximately here because plan-once is approximately sequential, bound J_pi/J_TR - 1 by the gain-weighted mean relative regret. Calibrate the bound on local information (regret 0.154 corresponds to x1.02), so the decision-level gates gain an outcome-level meaning.

Gibbs soft-target regret bound. For p* proportional to exp(-r/tau) over K actions, E_p*[r] <= (K-1) tau / e, which is 0.013 at tau = 0.005 for K = 8. The training target is therefore itself planner-quality, matching target risk's own Monte Carlo-noise regret of 0.013-0.016.

agenda.thesis: A language model can beat a numerical experimental-design planner only by supplying something the planner lacks: information that exists only in language or pretraining, a better model class, candidates outside the planner's set, or a better approximation where exact planning is intractable. With equal information, a correct model and a tractable Bayes planner it provably cannot win. The completed 24-system screen was in that regime: adaptivity is exactly worthless in its design-only subclass and was measured at -0.7% +/- 1.7% overall, so any legitimate LLM advantage was capped at roughly 2% of final risk. If results are positive, the paper claims that a trained LLM intervention policy that reads textual domain information (which causal links are absent, or how mechanisms bend) captured a calibrated share of the computed information value on fresh systems, beat the strongest numerical controls that lacked the text (uninformed planner, law-aware planner, GO-CBED-style amortized policy), scaled its benefit with the controlled information dose, showed no benefit where theory predicts none, and never exceeded the oracle-informed ceiling. If results are null or negative, the paper is a theory-and-measurement contribution: a sequential value-gap decomposition whose terms are computable numerical arms, theorems explaining why adaptive or learned policies cannot win in conjugate known-graph classes, a headroom atlas showing where an LLM could win, a calibrated instrument (endpoint, power, ceiling audit) for LLM-for-design claims, and the documented finding that the LLM did not turn text into better interventions at this scale. If the compiler arm succeeds where the policy fails, the claim narrows to the LLM as an information source for a numerical planner.

experiments.name: Value-gap decomposition of the completed 24-system screen
experiments.question: How large was each gap term (decision noise, myopia, adaptivity, omission, missing information) between target risk and the best achievable policy in the completed class, and so what was the largest advantage any policy could legitimately have shown?
experiments.design: Inputs: saved post-initialization states of all 24 development systems (identical across arms), saved action sequences of all 8 arms, 560 target-risk receipts, private world descriptors (development, post hoc). Reference arms, all model-internal with zero environment responses: R0 target risk as run (32 draws); R1 target risk with 4,096 draws and common random numbers across actions; R2 plan-once multiset optimum; R3 rollout planner (one-step lookahead over a target-risk base, 64 rollouts to budget end); R4 clairvoyant design (true theta in the shared learner's risk); R5 law-informed planner on the 12 shifted systems (knows edge mean 1.5, minimizes the shared learner's truth-law risk); R6 extended menu with the omitted bounds +/-2; R7 best leave-one-out state-blind schedule; R8 EPIG. Endpoints: (a) working-model design quality J from the common state, (b) truth-conditional expected final NMSE with redrawn noise and the true theta, (c) LLM arms' decision-level relative regret against the 16,384-draw reference, split into a state-blind component and a residual. n = 24, fixed by the completed screen. Paired log SD 0.035 for near-equal designs gives SE about 0.007, which resolves terms of 2% or more; MC SE of J is about 0.3% at 4,000 draws.
experiments.decision_rule: Predeclared. (i) No-headroom verdict if the upper 95% bound of (R0 - min(R1..R4))/R0 is below 5% on matched systems. (ii) If R3 beats R1 by 5% or more with lower CI above 0, a non-myopic control becomes mandatory everywhere and the greedy-optimality claim is narrowed. (iii) If Delta_info (R5 vs R1, endpoint b) is 5% or more, prior-shift class C1 is kept at n_init = 8 in E4; otherwise C1 is tested only at low n_init. (iv) If Delta_omission (R6 vs R1) is 15% or more, successor menus include boundary actions, decided now on LLM-independent grounds. Positive (no headroom) licenses 'the November null was predicted; no policy could exceed about 2 to 5% over target risk in this class'. Null or negative (headroom of 5% or more) licenses 'the null reflects endpoint and power, not absence of headroom', with no rerun of the old study.
experiments.prerequisites: Saved local files only. Reuse the validated independent replay (numerics-protocol acelib.py, which matches the saved curves to 1e-14). No approvals, no CURC.
experiments.cost: Zero environment responses. About 1 to 2 local CPU-hours (rollouts dominate) and 3 to 5 analyst-days. Basis: the numerics-protocol agent already ran 4,000-draw designs over the 24 saved states locally.
experiments.main_risk: Rollout and greedy references are approximate, so the no-headroom verdict could overstate. Mitigated by also bounding with the clairvoyant design.

experiments.name: Theory validation: adaptivity and greedy optimality in both directions
experiments.question: Do the formal predictions hold numerically: exactly zero adaptivity in the design-only subclass, adaptivity bounded by the clairvoyant EVPI and growing as initial information shrinks, greedy near-optimal where the submodularity ratio is near 1, and the side-information formula matching simulation?
experiments.design: Fresh synthetic development systems from a frozen namespace; linear-Gaussian with known noise; model-internal; no LLM. S0, design-only subclass: chain or fork with only actions that clamp the target head's parents and linear queries (do(Y) for Z in the chain, do(X) in the fork); budget 24, unit costs; exact multiset optimum by enumeration (at most 2,925 multisets). S1, completed-class mechanics: 3-node chain, fork and collider with the 8-action menu at n_init in {0,1,2,4,8,16} and noise variance in {0.25,1}. S2: 5-node random DAG at n_init in {0,2,8}. Arms: target risk (4,096 draws, common random numbers), plan-once, rollout (adaptive non-myopic), clairvoyant, random, best leave-one-out static schedule. Quantities: V_adapt = (J_OL - J_rollout)/J_OL; EVPI_design = (J_OL - J_clair)/J_OL; greedy vs best multiset; submodularity ratio gamma on small budgets; analytic vs simulated design value of side information for linear targets. 48 systems per cell (S0 48; S1 12 x 48; S2 3 x 48). SE about 0.005 on the mean log ratio at SD 0.035 resolves 1.5% at z about 3. Endpoint: expected final posterior NMSE (exact here because the truth law equals the prior).
experiments.decision_rule: P1: in S0, |J_adaptive - J_best_multiset| <= 2 MC SE in at least 95% of systems, else stop (bug or theory error) and fix before anything else. P2: V_adapt at n_init = 0 exceeds V_adapt at n_init = 8 by at least 3 points (paired lower 95% CI above 0) and V_adapt <= EVPI_design + 2 SE in at least 90% of systems; then the initial-information explanation of the null stands. If V_adapt is about 0 at every n_init, the null is stronger and E4 must look to structure or misspecification. If V_adapt exceeds EVPI_design systematically, the theory section is narrowed to empirical statements. P3: greedy attains at least (1 - e^-gamma) of the best multiset everywhere; report the empirical ratios. P4: analytic vs simulated side-information value within 10%. Positive licenses the theory section with numerical verification; null or negative narrows it.
experiments.prerequisites: In-process vectorized planner (removes the one-process-per-decision artefact behind the 48 s numerical episodes). Raise the 256-draw cap and add common random numbers to target_risk. Small protocol module for n_init and new graphs. Rollout planner. Written protocol with frozen namespaces. No CURC, no LLM.
experiments.cost: About 5 to 15 local CPU-hours [assumption: 10 to 50 ms per vectorized decision, rollouts 64 to 512 times that]. 1.5 to 2 engineer-weeks, shared with E3 and E4.
experiments.main_risk: Optimization error in the references can confound the inequality checks. Mitigated by exact enumeration in S0 and small-budget exact DP on a subset.

experiments.name: Equal-information numerical control suite and its qualification
experiments.question: Do numerical controls that receive exactly the LLM's information (state, generator law, text in oracle or parsed form) reach their theoretically computable values, so that every later LLM contrast is against strong, correctly implemented controls?
experiments.design: Implement and qualify on development states. C1: uninformed planner, target risk at 1,024 to 4,096 draws with common random numbers (the 'planner' from here on). C2: EPIG (Bickford Smith et al. 2023). C3: non-myopic rollout planner, plus exact multiset or DP planner where T1 applies. C4: oracle-informed planner; knows the side information numerically and minimizes the shared learner's truth-law risk; for sparsity classes it draws fantasy truths from the true-subgraph learner while scoring the shared supergraph learner. C5: law-aware planner; knows the generator law (spike-and-slab over at most 8 subgraphs, closed-form marginal likelihoods) but has no text. C6: reliability-aware text planner, a mixture prior with the true text reliability r (Bayes-optimal user of the text, and the privileged teacher for E7). C7: rule-based text parser plus C4, written from the training phrasing families only, before any LLM scoring. C8: GO-CBED-style amortized goal-oriented transformer policy over the same numeric state, in no-text and parsed-text variants, trained on the training namespace with a 1x, 4x, 16x budget sweep; also the public GO-CBED code if approved. C9: semantic-feature numerical policy (numeric features plus a frozen-LLM text embedding) trained on the LLM's data (Gupta et al. control). C10: best leave-one-out static schedule, and random. Sample: 48 development systems x 8 states per qualifying cell.
experiments.decision_rule: Qualification is predeclared. C1: median top-two gap at least 2 MC SE in at least 75% of decisions. C4: reaches the computed Delta_info ceiling within MC error. C5: at least as good as C1 on structure-uncertain cells. C8: design quality within 5% of C1 (no text) on held-out development states at some budget up to 16x, with the learning curve reported; if never within 5%, it is labelled an under-trained comparator and the paper may not claim 'beats amortized numerical policies'. C9: at least 90% held-in text-to-structure accuracy, otherwise labelled under-powered. A control enters later studies only if it qualifies; failures are preserved and reported. Positive licenses the strong-control requirement (submission conditions 2 and 3). Negative means the control is fixed or the claim is narrowed.
experiments.prerequisites: E2 machinery. Per-coefficient prior means and variances inside the planner's internal model only; the shared learner is unchanged. Lead approval to download GO-CBED code, or an in-house reimplementation. Approval for local training or inference for C8 and C9 (C9 executes a frozen model).
experiments.cost: 2 to 3 engineer-weeks; 5 to 20 local CPU-hours. C8 training 1 to 4 GPU-hours or 10 to 30 local CPU/MPS hours [assumption; GO-CBED's own budget unverified]. C9 embeddings: one forward pass per text at 0.4 to 0.7 s, under 1 h.
experiments.main_risk: A reimplemented GO-CBED may be judged unfaithful by reviewers. Mitigated by using the public code if approved and reporting the training-budget curve.

experiments.name: Headroom atlas and LLM-independent class selection
experiments.question: In which expressible classes, and at which controlled doses, is there verified headroom between the strongest no-text numerical control and the ceiling reachable with information or a model the planner lacks, large enough to detect at a feasible sample size?
experiments.design: Numerical arms only (E3 suite), development namespaces, design-only mode with one shared learner. C1 prior-mean shift: delta in {0,1.5,3} x n_init in {0,2,8} x noise variance in {0.25,1}. C2 known supergraph with sparse truth and text naming absent edges: 4- or 5-node supergraphs with known topological order, absent-edge fraction in {0,1/3,2/3} x text reliability r in {1,0.8} x n_init in {0,2,8} x noise variance in {0.25,1}; menus include clamp-at-zero joint actions. C4 indivisible costs: most-informative-action cost ratio kappa in {1,2,4,8} x n_init in {2,8}, with budget remainders. Query laws vary across systems in all classes. Arms: C1, C5, C8 (no text), static, random, and the ceilings C4, C6 and C3. Endpoints: truth-conditional expected log final NMSE at fixed budget; cost-equivalent saving; predicted n for the LLM contrast. 48 systems per cell (about 60 cells, about 2,900 systems), R = 2 trajectories with common random numbers. At the worst observed SD (0.24) the SE at n = 48 is 0.035, which resolves a 10% gap at z about 2.7.
experiments.decision_rule: Predeclared before any LLM is scored on any class, and independent of LLM performance. A class qualifies at a dose if (i) the ceiling gap G (strongest no-text control vs ceiling) is at least log 1.10 with lower 95% CI at least log 1.05; (ii) the predicted n to detect G/2 at alpha 0.05/3 two-sided with 90% power, using the cell's paired SD inflated 1.5x for LLM noise, is at most 96 systems; (iii) its zero-dose anchor has |G| < 2%; (iv) G rises across doses. Select at most two classes: largest G at feasible n, then smaller code change, then relevance to the experimentalist task. If none qualifies, LLM superiority work stops and the paper becomes theory plus atlas plus diagnostics; the negative result narrows the claim, and no other benchmark may be adopted without a new LLM-independent justification of this kind. Predictions: C1 small except at n_init <= 2, noise variance 1, delta 3; C2 large (two-coefficient toy gives true-risk ratio 0.26 to 0.36); C4 nonzero only for kappa > 1 and closed by DP, so it can host only a mechanism test (E9).
experiments.prerequisites: E2 and E3 machinery. Protocol modules for C1, C2 and C4. A sparse truth law for C2: exact zeros on supergraph edges needs either a world-descriptor schema change (coefficient SD is one scalar today) or a world graph distinct from the public graph; whether the assembler enforces graph equality is unverified. Frozen namespaces and a written protocol.
experiments.cost: 20 to 60 local CPU-hours [assumption: about 40,000 in-process episodes at 1 to 5 s; law-aware and rollout arms dominate]. 1 to 2 engineer-weeks after E2 and E3. No CURC.
experiments.main_risk: Dilution: the first-order effect of absent-edge information seen in the toy may shrink in realistic supergraphs, and the selection thresholds are judgment calls that must be frozen before running.

experiments.name: Instrument calibration with synthetic policies of known capture
experiments.question: Before any LLM is scored, does the planned endpoint, analysis and sample size recover a known information-capture ratio without bias, with nominal error rates and a working ceiling audit?
experiments.design: In the selected class or classes, on development systems. Synthetic policies: pi_rho takes C4's action with probability rho and C1's otherwise (rho in {0,0.25,0.5,1}), with capture defined on the value scale and the rho-to-capture mapping calibrated here; a text-trusting state-blind schedule; a leakage policy that reads the private truth and should exceed the ceiling; a feedback-blind copy of C1, to measure the power of the shuffled-feedback control as a function of V_adapt. Run the complete planned E10 analysis: paired primary endpoint, R = 2 with common random numbers, dose-response regression of benefit on the E4-predicted gap, placebo non-superiority, Holm. Sample: the planned confirmation size (156 systems) repeated over 20 independent namespace draws or 200 system-bootstrap resamples.
experiments.decision_rule: Pass requires all of: |rho_hat - rho| <= 0.1 for all rho; 95% CI coverage between 0.92 and 0.98; power at least 80% at rho = 0.5; false-positive rate at most 5% at rho = 0 and in the placebo; leakage policy flagged in at least 95% of draws; design-quality and realized-error endpoints agree in sign in at least 90% of draws at rho >= 0.5. On failure, change n, replicates or endpoint now, never after LLM scoring. Positive licenses capture-ratio claims with calibrated intervals. Negative means the confirmation cannot test the claim and must be redesigned.
experiments.prerequisites: E3 and E4 complete; analysis code frozen.
experiments.cost: 2 to 6 local CPU-hours and 3 to 5 analyst-days. No LLM, no CURC.
experiments.main_risk: Decision-level mixing is nonlinear in value; handled by calibrating the mapping inside this experiment.

experiments.name: Zero-shot information-use probe on frozen local models
experiments.question: Does any locally cached frozen model shift its choices toward what the side information warrants on states where that information changes the optimal action, and leave them unchanged otherwise?
experiments.design: Offline states from the selected class (development namespace): 64 systems x 6 states. Text conditions: absent, correct, shuffled (another system's hint), misleading; plus content-free state controls and menu-order and identifier permutations. Models: Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (all in the local HF cache). Prompt: compact rounded posterior summary, text and menu; no planner scores. Scoring: whole-command log-probabilities (length-normalized and raw), not greedy trie decoding; thinking off vs on for Qwen3. Labels: C1 vs C4 rankings at 4,096 draws with common random numbers. Switch states are those where the informed-best action differs from the uninformed-best by at least 2 MC SE. Endpoints: Delta_switch = P(informed best | correct text) - P(informed best | text absent) on switch states; the same on non-switch states; regret under the truth-law risk; bootstrap by system. About 384 states per condition, from 2 x ((1.96 + 0.84) x 0.5/0.1)^2 = 392 (binomial SD 0.5, clustering design effect 2).
experiments.decision_rule: A model uses the information if Delta_switch >= 0.10 with CI excluding 0, misleading text moves choices away from the informed best by at least 0.05, shuffled text gives |Delta| <= 0.05, and non-switch accuracy drops by no more than 0.05. Predicted: null for 0.6B, possibly positive for 7B. Positive at 0.6B means E7 can focus on decisions rather than reading. Positive only at 7B means capacity is the bottleneck and larger-model training becomes an ask. Null for all models means training must teach reading and the paper makes no zero-shot claims.
experiments.prerequisites: Lead approval for local forward-only inference, including the 7B weights. E4 class selection. Frozen prompt format and whole-command scoring code.
experiments.cost: No CURC. About 5,000 to 6,000 scorings at about 1 to 2 s (0.6B, 1.5B) and 3 to 6 s (7B) on the M5 Max, so 4 to 10 h wall [assumption; the GPU slice took 0.4 to 0.7 s per 0.6B decision on 2,000 to 4,000-token prompts]. 2 to 3 analyst-days.
experiments.main_risk: Prompt-surface sensitivity, which dominated every past LLM arm. Mitigated by permutations and whole-command scoring.

experiments.name: Trained LLM policy on the information channel: development dose-response
experiments.question: Does a trained LLM action policy capture a predicted share of the information value, with benefit tracking the computed dose, vanishing where theory says it must, bounded harm and recovery under misleading text, and a win over the strongest numerical control that lacks the text?
experiments.design: Training on the selected class's training namespace. Targets: graded listwise softmax of the privileged teacher C6's scores, on states visited by a teacher-student mixture (DAgger-style relabelling), with per-example identifier and menu permutation. Hint texts from human-written phrasing families, split into training and held-out families and frozen before training. The recipe comes from the training workstream; any recipe that passes the gates is acceptable, and Kriz et al.'s on-policy GRPO is the literature baseline. LLM arms: L1 policy (text plus numeric state, no planner scores); L2 re-ranker over C1's top 3 with scores, plus an argmax-of-prompt baseline; L3 LLM compiler (text to structure vector) plus C4; L4 L1 without text; L5 L1 with shuffled text; L6 same architecture without language pretraining (or C9 if infeasible). Numerical arms: C1, C5, C8 (both variants), C7, the ceilings C4 and C6, static, random. Gates before episodes: G-state, where on no-text states L1's decision-level relative regret beats the best state-blind schedule and captures at least 25% of the plan-once-vs-static gap; G-text, Delta_switch >= 0.20 on held-out phrasing families. Episodes: E4 zero, mid and high doses, a misleading-text cell and a no-information placebo cell; 48 development systems per cell; R = 2 with common random numbers. Shuffled-feedback control (L1 with permuted measured values) in the cell with the largest V_adapt. Endpoints: primary truth-conditional expected log final NMSE; cost-equivalent saving; realized error; recovery delay (acquisitions until the first probe of a claimed-absent edge, compared with C6). Analysis: regression of paired benefit (L1 vs C1, C5 and C8) on the predicted gap.
experiments.decision_rule: Development rules, predeclared. Advance to E10 only if all hold: benefit slope on the predicted gap has lower 90% CI above 0; rho_hat >= 0.3 at high dose; zero-dose and placebo benefit <= +2% and at most the ceiling; L1 (or the predeclared L2) beats the strongest no-text control by at least 5% at high dose; misleading-text harm is no worse than a fully trusting planner's and recovery delay is at most twice C6's. Kill if rho_hat <= 0.1 or L1 is more than 5% worse than C1 at zero dose. Outcomes: positive means freeze and confirm. L3 >= L1 confirms T4 and makes the confirmable claim 'the LLM contributes by reading information into the decision', with the lead choosing the role before E10. Null licenses 'the LLM did not turn textual information into decisions at this scale' and the claim narrows. Negative (worse than C1 even with correct text) redirects the method to L2 or a larger model; the benchmark is never changed.
experiments.prerequisites: E3 to E5 passed (E6 informative, not required). New GPU ceiling. Training-workstream recipe. Text families and development protocol frozen before training.
experiments.cost: Training 2 to 6 GPU-slice-hours: 8,000 listwise updates at 0.62 s is about 1.4 h, and 250 on-policy updates with 128 single-decision rollouts add 1 to 4 h [assumption: batched generation]. Development evaluation: 48 x 5 cells x 2 reps x 3 LLM arms x 24 decisions is about 34,560 decisions at 0.4 to 0.7 s, so 3.8 to 6.7 h (L4 to L6 can be scored at decision level only to reduce this). Numerical arms 5 to 20 CPU-hours in-process. Total about 6 to 13 slice-hours, far above the remaining 2,742 slice-seconds. 3 to 4 weeks.
experiments.main_risk: L1 fails G-state (numeric-state reading), as every past LLM arm did, leaving only the narrower L2 and L3 roles.

experiments.name: Misspecification class: curvature dose-response and wind-tunnel simulator transfer
experiments.question: When the planner's linear model is misspecified in a way that language or pretrained physics can describe, does the LLM capture a predicted share of Delta_misspec, with no benefit at zero curvature, and does that transfer to a physics simulator family?
experiments.design: Stage A (numerical): nonlinear truth (quadratic or saturating, curvature gamma in {0,0.25,0.5,1}) with a shared linear learner; operating-point queries off the menu (for example x* = 1.5) and a 9-level action grid on [-2,2]. Arms: linear planner, oracle-informed planner (knows the form and the gamma law), robust model-averaging planner (linear, quadratic, cubic bases; no text), GO-CBED-style. Same gate as E4, 48 systems per cell. Prediction: extreme designs optimal at gamma = 0, so inward moves are harmful there (negative control); local designs win at gamma > 0 (Box-Draper bias-variance trade-off). Stage B (LLM, only if Stage A qualifies): E7 recipe trained on synthetic curvature families with physics-style text; dose-response on gamma including gamma = 0 with text saying 'linear'. Stage C (transfer): causalchamber wind-tunnel simulators (affinity-law fan speed, cubic current, squared-speed pressure, linear hatch term) with the documented prose descriptions. Controls: linear planner, physics-basis planner using the published models (well-specified ceiling), robust planner. 48 simulated systems from parameters randomized within documented ranges; claim scope stated as one simulator family.
experiments.decision_rule: Stage A gate as in E4. Stage B as in E7: slope > 0, gamma = 0 benefit <= +2%, rho_hat >= 0.3. Stage C: report rho_hat relative to the physics ceiling with a system-bootstrap CI; positive if the lower CI is above 0 and the LLM beats the robust no-text planner. Positive partly meets submission condition 4 (transfer beyond the synthetic generator). Null means the misspecification decomposition is reported without an LLM claim. Negative at gamma = 0 documents a calibrated-trust failure.
experiments.prerequisites: Nonlinear mechanisms, a redefined estimand (expected response, since the noise-disabled structural mean is not the expected response under nonlinearity) and evaluator: a medium change. Basis learner for the planner's internal model. pip install causalchamber (approval). E7 recipe for Stage B.
experiments.cost: 2 to 4 engineer-weeks. Stage A 10 to 30 local CPU-hours. Stage B about E7's GPU cost (6 to 13 slice-hours) unless training is shared across classes. Stage C CPU only (numpy simulators).
experiments.main_risk: A simple numerical locality rule may capture most of the misspecification headroom, leaving nothing language-specific to win.

experiments.name: Non-myopic budget class: bounded benefit against the myopic planner, none against DP
experiments.question: Can a trained LLM capture non-myopic value (budget remainders, indivisible costs) that the one-step ratio planner misses, with a benefit bounded by the exact DP control as the equal-information ceiling requires?
experiments.design: Indivisible-cost class C4 with kappa in {1,2,4,8}, design-only subclass where exact DP over action-count vectors is computable (T1 part 3). Arms: myopic target risk, DP or multiset optimum, rollout, LLM trained on DP budget-to-go targets, LLM trained on one-step targets (ablation), GO-CBED-style. 48 development systems per kappa; decision-level and episode-level endpoints as in E7.
experiments.decision_rule: Predicted: all arms equal at kappa = 1 (anchor); LLM_multi - myopic <= DP - myopic; one-step-trained LLM captures about 0. 'Learned budget-aware planning' may be claimed only if rho_hat >= 0.5 with CI above 0 and rho_hat(one-step) < rho_hat(multi-step). Superiority over DP is impossible; an apparent advantage beyond MC error triggers the leakage audit.
experiments.prerequisites: E4 shows C4 headroom against the myopic planner. DP planner. GPU allocation.
experiments.cost: 2 to 4 GPU-slice-hours, reusing E7 infrastructure; under 10 CPU-hours.
experiments.main_risk: Low payoff for the headline: by construction it cannot show superiority over the strongest control.

experiments.name: Fresh-system confirmation with dose and placebo strata
experiments.question: On fresh systems with frozen methods, namespaces, endpoints and failure treatment, does the LLM role carried from E7 beat the strongest no-text numerical control, with benefit tracking the predicted dose, none where theory predicts none, and no gain beyond the computed ceiling?
experiments.design: Fresh confirmation namespace in the selected class. Strata: high dose 36, mid dose 36, zero dose 36 (in-class placebo), misleading text 24, completed-regime placebo 24 (fresh systems in the new pipeline, not a rerun); 156 systems, R = 2 replicates with common random numbers. Arms (up to 10, so the 8-policy roster limit must be raised): frozen LLM role from E7, C1 (4,096 draws with common random numbers), C5, C8 (best no-text variant fixed on development data), C7, ceilings C4 and C6, static, random. Primary endpoint: truth-conditional expected log final NMSE at fixed budget, averaged over replicates. Secondary: cost-equivalent saving from the planner's expected error-cost curve, realized-error agreement, public-stopping cost with reliability, recovery delay. Hypotheses (Holm, k = 3): H1, LLM beats the strongest no-text control on pooled high and mid strata; H2, positive dose-response slope with zero-dose benefit upper 95% bound <= 5%; H3, placebo gain upper bound <= computed ceiling + 5% and a clean leakage audit. Sample basis: a 10% effect (half of a verified gap of at least 20%) at paired SD 0.15 to 0.20 with Holm k = 3 and 90% power needs 34 to 60 systems; 72 are planned in the pooled informative strata, and n is raised before the freeze if E5 says so.
experiments.decision_rule: The superiority claim requires H1 and H2 after Holm, plus H3. If H1 passes but H3 fails, no claim is made until the leakage audit resolves. If H1 fails, the claim narrows to development-only evidence, no benchmark is substituted, and the paper reports the theory, the atlas and the failed confirmation. In every case failures are preserved, responses are accounted for and an independent review is done.
experiments.prerequisites: E7 pass. Custody redesign (brief section 5). Raised roster limits. Lift the arm-namespace rule to allow common random numbers. New compute ceiling. Frozen protocol hash and analysis code. An independent reviewer.
experiments.cost: LLM: 156 x 2 x (1 or 2 LLM arms) x 24 is about 7,500 to 15,000 decisions at 0.4 to 0.7 s, so 0.8 to 2.9 GPU-slice-hours plus service overhead. CPU: the brief's 22 to 35 core-hours for 100 to 150 systems is an upper bound (it includes the subprocess artefact); in-process numerics cost far less. 2 to 3 weeks including custody.
experiments.main_risk: Shrinkage from development to fresh systems; development rankings reversed on fresh systems twice before in this project.

Weeks 1 to 4: E2 and E3 in parallel on a shared in-process vectorized planner; E4 starts once E2's P1 check (exact zero adaptivity in the design-only subclass) passes, around weeks 3 to 5. Gate A, LLM-independent class selection by E4's predeclared criteria: if no class qualifies, LLM superiority work stops and the theory, atlas and diagnostics paper is written; only that version can meet ICML on 22 January 2027. Weeks 5 to 6: E5 (instrument calibration) and E6 (zero-shot probe, after the local-inference approval) in parallel; E8 Stage A and the numerical part of E9 may also run here. Gate B: the instrument must be validated before any LLM episode is scored. Weeks 6 to 10: E7, needing a new GPU ceiling. Gate C: E7's development criteria. Weeks 10 to 13: freeze methods, namespaces, endpoints and failure treatment, then run E10; E8 Stages B and C are optional in parallel if resources allow. The full agenda fits NeurIPS 2027 (estimated May) or TMLR; UAI (estimated February) is tight.

Do not rerun the 24-system study or the old pipelines; the completed-regime placebo in E10 consists of fresh systems in the new pipeline.
