experiments.name: Imitation ladder with knockouts and matched numerical students (gates use training-side data only)
experiments.question: Can a Qwen3-0.6B policy trained with a repaired recipe read SCM state well enough to imitate target-risk planning on held-out systems? Which repairs are necessary? And does a numerical student trained on identical data do the same?
experiments.design:
Class: the completed 3-variable generator, drawn from a fresh declared training namespace. No development system or outcome is used. The planner's choices there depend strongly on state, so imitation is not trivial: the best state-blind first action has a relative regret of 0.257, the fixed coverage cycle 0.441 over whole episodes, and the constant set_x_neg policy 0.699.

Data:
- 400 training worlds giving about 9,600 states, from a mix of behavior policies (random, coverage, local information, target risk);
- repetition-stress histories with 10 to 23 repeated actions;
- the 697 saved training envelopes;
- labels: 4,096-draw target-risk scores for all 8 actions, which cost no environment responses.

Held out: 80 further training-namespace worlds, evaluated on each student's own closed-loop rollouts.

Arms:
- A1, full repair:
  - graded listwise KL to a softmax of planner scores, at a temperature fixed in the protocol;
  - a rounded, decision-relevant SCM summary of about 400 to 700 tokens, with no scores per action;
  - neutral identifiers, with identifiers and menu order permuted per example;
  - whole-command normalized scoring;
  - 2 shuffled epochs, rank-16 LoRA on the attention and MLP projections.
- A2: A1 without the posterior summary (history only).
- A3: hard argmax labels.
- A4: labels from the November rule (4 replicates, 2-SE tie rule) on the same states.
- A5: fixed menu order and the original identifiers.
- A6: the raw November JSON envelope with 17-digit floats, on half the data.
- A7: A1's weights decoded token by token greedily (no training).
- N1: an MLP on the same numeric summary, trained on A1's targets.
- N2: N1 trained on A4's labels.
- References: a state-blind frequency counter; target risk, local information, coverage and random; the November ranker, SFT and DPO adapters.

Seeds: 3 for A1, A2, N1 and N2; 2 for A3 to A5; 1 for A6.

Primary endpoint: mean relative regret on the held-out rollouts under the 16,384-draw target-risk score. Secondary: cross-entropy relative to the counter, action entropy, total-variation change under state shuffling, and the model-expected final NMSE J relative to target risk.

Sample basis: the November regret contrasts imply a per-world SD of about 0.28, so 80 worlds give an SE of about 0.031 and a regret difference of 0.10 has z of about 3.2. Using 2 or 3 seeds answers the single-seed limitation flagged by Kriz et al.
experiments.decision_rule:
Gate: an arm "learns state-dependent SCM planning" only if, in every seed, all four hold:
- regret <= 0.154 (the level local information reached);
- cross-entropy at least 0.2 nats per example better than the counter;
- total-variation change under state shuffling >= 0.2, with world-cluster permutation p < 0.01;
- J within 10% of target risk.

Outcomes:
- A1 passes and N1 passes: the recipe is repaired and branch P may use it. This licenses "language pretraining is not needed for imitation, so any LLM benefit must come from text".
- A1 passes and N1 fails: an unexpected advantage from the language representation. Replicate before claiming it.
- A1 fails and N1 passes: the 0.6B LLM is the bottleneck under offline distillation, so run E4. If E4 also fails, kill K2 closes the direct LLM policy.
- Both fail: the supervision or the state design is insufficient, and the paper is the diagnostic one.

Knockouts:
- A component is necessary if removing it raises regret by at least 0.10 in every seed.
- A4 and N2 "reproduce the collapse" if one action exceeds 80% of choices or the action entropy falls below 0.8 bits. If both collapse, the paper may say the collapse comes from the supervision, not from language.
- A1 versus A2 is the ablation of the SCM state.

No outcome on the 24 development systems is touched.
experiments.cost:
- Training: 13 LoRA runs. A summary-prompt run is about 4,000 states x 2 epochs x 600 tokens x 1.5 (listwise overhead), or about 7.2 M tokens. At the measured throughput of about 5,000 tokens per second on the slice, that is about 0.4 to 0.55 slice-hours per run. The raw-envelope arm takes about 1.0 to 1.3 hours. Total: about 6 to 9 slice-hours, or 1 to 3 nights on the Mac (throughput there is unmeasured).
- Relabeling: 5 to 10 CPU-hours.
- Held-out rollouts: about 27,000 decisions, or 1 to 2 GPU-hours.
- Calendar: about 3 weeks.
experiments.main_risk: The summary text or the temperature may quietly encode the planner's answer. This is mitigated by never including scores per action. Alternatively, a 0.6B model may fail whatever the recipe.

experiments.name: Escalation: model capacity versus on-policy training (runs only if E3 shows A1 failing and N1 passing)
experiments.question: Is the 0.6B LLM's failure to imitate the planner caused by model capacity or by offline supervision?
experiments.design:
The same data, held-out worlds and gates as E3.
- Arm (a), capacity: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, already in the local cache, with the A1 recipe, 2 seeds.
- Arm (b), on-policy training: Qwen3-0.6B with on-policy GRPO, using the settings Kriz et al. report for the same base model: 16 states x 16 rollouts per update, 250 updates, temperature 2, an entropy bonus of 0.02, and permuted identifiers. The reward is the sampled action's 256-draw one-step target-risk gain per unit cost. 2 seeds.

The held-out regret endpoint and the secondary metrics are the same as in E3.
experiments.decision_rule:
An arm passes on E3's gates.
- 7B passes: capacity was the bottleneck. Branch P continues with 7B, and its inference cost goes into the compute ablation.
- GRPO passes: offline distillation was the bottleneck. Branch P continues with GRPO.
- Both fail (kill K2): the direct LLM policy closes. The hybrid knowledge-compiler framing remains only if E1 admitted a class. Otherwise the paper is the diagnostic one.

Every outcome is reported as part of the anatomy.
experiments.prerequisites:
- Runs only if E3 ends with A1 failing and N1 passing.
- The lead's approval to use the cached 7B weights. No download is needed.
- GRPO implemented in the torch-only engine, about 1 to 2 weeks.
- Compute approval, either local or a CURC ceiling.
experiments.cost:
- GRPO: about 64,000 single-decision generations at 0.1 to 0.5 s, or about 2 to 9 GPU-hours, plus backward passes.
- 7B LoRA: 2 runs, each about 5 to 10 times as long as a 0.6B run, or 1 to 3 nights locally. The bf16 7B weights (about 15 GB) fit in 36 GB [judgment].
- Calendar: 2 to 3 weeks.

experiments.name: Development pilot in the admitted class (LLM variants trained by privileged-teacher distillation, against controls with the same information)
experiments.question: In the class E1 admitted, does an SCM-conditioned LLM that reads the prose choose interventions with lower truth-conditional error than the strongest numerical planner without the text? And does it beat a rule parser and a numerical student given the same information?
experiments.design:
Training: 400 worlds from a fresh training namespace in the admitted class. The teacher is O, which knows the true objective or prior. The students see only the public prose (families A and B) plus the SCM summary.

Systems: 48 fresh development-namespace systems, with 4 replicates and common random numbers. Prose comes from held-out family C, and from D if available.

Arms:
- U, O and R.
- L-dir: the direct LLM policy, using the E3 or E4 recipe plus the prose.
- L-hyb: the LLM maps the prose to the objective or prior as structured output, and U plans with it.
- L-adj: the prompt adds U's scores for each action, and the LLM chooses.
- N-emb: an MLP on the SCM summary plus a frozen LLM embedding of the prose, distilled from O.
- N-bow: the same with bag-of-words text features and no pretrained model.
- F: the frozen Qwen3-0.6B, zero-shot, with the same prompt.
- Random and coverage.

Ablations for each LLM variant, on a prespecified 24 of the 48 systems with 2 replicates:
- text removed;
- misleading text;
- shuffled feedback (responses permuted in the policy's input only);
- no SCM state;
- for L-adj, an argmax-of-prompt control.

Endpoint: the E1 primary. Secondary: oracle-gap closure, (U - L)/(U - O).

Sample basis: 48 systems estimate the paired SD for E6 to within about +/-10%, and gap closure with an SE of about 0.12 (for a gap of 0.3 log units and a paired SD of 0.25). That is enough to apply a 30% qualification threshold.
experiments.prerequisites:

- E3 or E4 produced a passing recipe.

- The lead's approval for training, either local or a compute ceiling.
- Roster limits raised.

- 6 LoRA runs (3 variants x 2 seeds), about 3 to 4 slice-hours.
- About 23,000 LLM decisions at 0.1 to 0.6 s, or 1 to 4 GPU-hours. L-hyb calls the LLM only once per system.
- Numerical arms: about 10 to 20 CPU-hours.
- Engineering about 2 weeks. Calendar about 3 weeks.

experiments.question: On systems never scored before, does the frozen LLM variant reduce truth-conditional cost or error compared with the strongest numerical planner without the text, and compared with the rule parser?

experiments.name: External transfer on the Causal Chambers wind-tunnel simulator
experiments.question: Does the frozen method's benefit carry over to a physical simulator written by independent authors, with documented misspecification and variable descriptions written by others?
experiments.design:
Simulator: an adapter over the causalchamber 0.2.8 wind-tunnel simulators. wt.SimA1C3 gives downwind pressure from load_in, load_out, hatch and ambient pressure. wt.ModelB1 gives current.
- Actions: actuators are discretized into at most 32 menu actions, each costing its settling time.
- Graph and text: the graph comes from the documentation. The prose comes from the official variable descriptions, plus experimentalist objectives in held-out wording.
- Learner: the linear SCM learner, which is misspecified by construction (affinity laws, a cubic current, and pressure that scales with speed squared).
- Instances: 40 simulator instances with physical parameters drawn from documented ranges, 4 replicates each.
- Arms: U, O, R, L* (frozen, not retrained) and N-emb.

Endpoint: the E1 primary, computed from the simulator's truth (noise-free outputs or many replicates).

Sample basis: at an SD of 0.25, 40 instances give about 98% power for a 15% effect and about 76% for a 10% effect (two-sided, 0.05).

Scope of the claim: one family of simulated apparatus.
experiments.decision_rule:
- Holds: the L*/U ratio <= 0.90 with the 95% CI below 1, and a sign that matches E6. This licenses "transfers to an independently authored, misspecified physical simulator".
- Partial: a point estimate <= 0.95 with a CI that includes 1. Reported as suggestive.
- Fails, otherwise (kill K5): the claim is restricted to synthetic classes, and no replacement simulator is searched.
experiments.prerequisites:
- The lead's approval to install causalchamber 0.2.8 (MIT), or to vendor its numpy-only wind-tunnel file. Version 1.0.0rc1 needs Python 3.11, and the local Python is 3.9.
- The frozen method. The adapter can be built while E6 runs.
experiments.cost: About 1 week of integration. About 13,000 decisions: at most 5 CPU-hours and about 1 to 2 GPU-hours. 1.5 to 2 weeks of calendar.
experiments.main_risk: Instances that differ only in parameters are correlated rather than independent systems. Under misspecification, stopping on posterior risk is miscalibrated; the reliability secondary detects this.

theory_items: T1, a ceiling on the value of adaptivity in conjugate known-graph linear-Gaussian design with clamp interventions. Each head's posterior covariance depends only on that head's design rows, so the value of sequential adaptation is bounded by how much the mean-dependent composed terms (mu_phi^T V mu_phi + m^T C_phi m) vary under the posterior predictive. When every query probes clamped parents, plan-once is Bayes-optimal (Chaloner and Verdinelli 1995). Why it helps: it turns the measured -0.7% +/- 1.7% into a general guideline for which classes can reward any learned policy, which every framing needs.

T2, an equal-information impossibility and a decomposition of excess loss. Under a correct model with the same information and objective, the Bayes sequential rule minimizes expected loss. Any policy's advantage therefore splits into four sources: information the planner lacks, the planner's approximation error (myopia, Monte Carlo error, the ratio heuristic), misspecification, and compute. This links to the agenda's kappa + 2 epsilon + delta. Why it helps: it makes E1's admission rule principled rather than a convenient choice of benchmark, and it states in advance what an LLM win can mean.

T3, efficiency of endpoints. Consider first-passage cost on an error process with a coefficient of variation near 1 and no common random numbers. The variance of a paired difference has a floor set by within-system noise, and truth-conditional expected error with common random numbers removes that floor. Deriving n under each endpoint reproduces the contrast of 67 to 340 versus 3 to 17 systems. Why it helps: it is a reusable methodological result and justifies the primary endpoint.

T4, label noise from replicate tie rules. With r replicates and a k-SE rule, the probability of a false strict label is P(|t_{r-1}| > k), which is 0.139 at r = 4 and k = 2. Combined with the measured distribution of gains, this predicts that 69 to 73% of strict labels are at chance. Through the robust-DPO factor 1/(1 - 2 epsilon), it predicts that preference learning fails. Why it helps: it explains the failure in the anatomy section and gives a design rule for how many replicates each label needs.

T5, the bias of greedy decoding over a command trie. Greedy prefix-constrained decoding picks the branch with the largest pooled probability at the first point where commands diverge. It departs from the whole-command argmax whenever max_c P(c) is below the pooled mass of a sibling group, which favors large command families such as the seven set_* commands against observe. Why it helps: it explains how SFT inflated set_x_neg, and it is a general warning for policies that use constrained decoding.

T6, the value of information that exists only in text. Under the true objective, J(U) - J(O) >= 0 bounds what any policy that reads the text can gain, gap closure is at most 1 in expectation, and the rule parser gives a lower bound on the share that needs no language understanding. Why it helps: it makes positive results readable as statements about information rather than as 'the LLM beats the planner'.

strongest_ideas: Equal-information ceiling (T4) plus a sequential value-gap decomposition (T5) whose terms are differences of computable numerical arms. A capture ratio above 1 triggers a leakage audit. This turns 'where can an LLM win' into an operational, LLM-independent question.
E1 decomposes the completed screen at zero environment cost (rollout, clairvoyant, law-informed and extended-menu references), turning Finding A into a quantitative bound.

E3 is a qualified equal-information control suite that matches what reviewers now demand: law-aware planner (C5), rule parser written before any LLM scoring (C7), GO-CBED-style amortized policy with a 1x/4x/16x training-budget sweep (C8), semantic-feature student (C9), and oracle-informed and reliability-aware ceilings.
E5 calibrates the instrument with synthetic policies of known capture (mixtures over rho, a leakage policy, a feedback-blind copy) before any LLM is scored. This is rare and decisive for credibility.
E7 and E10 test dose-response with zero-dose and completed-regime placebo strata, measure recovery delay under misleading text, and use T7 to show where shuffled-feedback controls have power at all.
The L3 compiler arm comes with an honest prediction that compiler plus planner will match or beat the direct policy.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: No training recipe and no learnability gate. E7 imports 'the recipe from the training workstream' although every past LLM arm collapsed, so the agenda is incomplete on what condition (1) requires. There are no forensics of the saved adapters, so the null paper lacks the collapse anatomy.

E10 lists only the trained LLM role plus numerical controls (advantage-theory.md:527). It omits the frozen base LLM and the supervised LLM that the standing rules require, and it has no training-seed replication.

The claim that 'a legitimate LLM win was capped at about 2% of final risk' is asserted before the rollout, DP and law-aware references exist. It holds in matched regimes against a Bayes rule, not for trained policies that learn the shifted generator law.

The engineering path is long: about 5 to 8 engineer-weeks before any LLM training. A 60-cell atlas of about 2,900 systems with 'largest G' selection invites a winner's curse. C2 needs a world-schema change and an unverified check that the assembler enforces graph equality.

Templated hints are parseable by construction, so the legitimate LLM edge rests on a few human-written phrasing families. Those families, not the systems, are the effective units, and the power analysis ignores this.
E9 cannot show superiority by construction. T1 to T3 are largely known results (Chaloner and Verdinelli, Das and Kempe, Golovin and Krause) and should be presented as tools, not contributions.

strongest_ideas: A complete decision tree: claims per branch (F1 positive policy, F2 compiler, F3 diagnostic, D delivery), predeclared kill criteria K1 to K6, venue mapping, and correction of the public README and arXiv record as a precondition.

The E1 admission rule has numeric thresholds and a rule-parser residual on held-out phrasing families. This is the cleanest LLM-independent definition of 'information that exists only in text'. The primary endpoint is frozen before any LLM sees the new classes.

E3 runs imitation on fresh training-namespace worlds against matched numerical students (including N2 trained on November-rule labels). Knockouts are tied to named mechanisms, and no development outcome is touched.

E5 compares three LLM roles (direct, hybrid compiler, adjudicator with an argmax-of-prompt deviation test) against N-emb and N-bow students, with text-removed, misleading-text, shuffled-feedback and no-SCM ablations and a single-variant promotion rule.

E6 has two primaries (against the uninformed planner and against the rule parser) under Holm, followed by external transfer to the independently authored wind-tunnel simulator. Hardware stays optional, and the calendar is realistic.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: The K1 'prose objective' class withholds the objective from the planner. Reviewers will call it a strawman unless the text truly resists parsing, which needs a human-written held-out family D that is not secured. Synthetic families A to C are probably parser-solvable.

There is no no-text law-aware (empirical-Bayes) planner and no no-text amortized student. A trained LLM learns the training generator's coefficient law, so a gain in K2 could come from that law rather than from the text.
The confirmation runs a single frozen L* and E5 uses two seeds per variant, so recipe variability is not estimated (the caveat Kriz et al. raise).
No evaluator validation (A/A size, planted effect, known-capture policies) before scoring. The endpoint is chosen from z-ratios alone.
E3 is heavy (13 LoRA runs, about 6 to 9 slice-hours, about 3 weeks). A6 (raw envelope) and A7 (greedy decoding) duplicate the E2 forensics.
Wind-tunnel transfer is scored on NMSE rather than an observable useful outcome, and E9 (delivery study) is outside this agenda.

strongest_ideas: Rao-Blackwellized truth-law evaluation (ERB) with stated validity conditions, plus a counterexample showing that the learner's posterior risk can be gamed under side information. This answers the circularity objection to model-based endpoints and sharply cuts the number of systems needed.
The harness is validated before any policy is scored: CRN keyed by action occurrence, A/A test size, planted-effect power, ERB unbiasedness, and agreement of paired-branch attribution.
A threshold-averaged band cost-to-target (T2) generalizes the declared endpoint instead of replacing it, with censoring and a public stop rule.

Confirmation discipline: K=5 seeds with at least 4 favorable, a TOST null branch, a Holm second-level family, blinding, fresh validation shards capped at three iterations, a failure ledger, and independent re-analysis with 10% re-execution.
The open-loop bound (T5) gives an outcome-based certificate of feedback use and a power argument for the shuffled-feedback control.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: Method-agnostic: classes and recipes come from an unspecified 'method panel', so the agenda alone cannot produce the paper or address condition (1).

E1 makes endpoint adoption depend partly on how the development LLM arms placed (a 'non-favorability' test). That breaks the letter of the rule that a benchmark or measurement change must rest on criteria independent of LLM performance, and the test has little bite because those arms were constant schedules.
Class qualification thresholds are in per-system SD units, which low-variance classes can meet with trivial natural-unit gains. Natural-unit minimum important differences are needed.
E9 Stage B runs hardware 'regardless of how the policies performed', which spends money and a human sign-up on a descriptive single-apparatus result.

No law-aware or LLM-compiler controls. Transfer families from the same codebase are weak evidence for condition (4). ERB is unavailable under misspecification, so its efficiency gain disappears exactly where transfer is tested.

strongest_ideas: E1: an in-process CRN planner that must reproduce all 560 saved receipts, a precision ladder, and an infinite-data ceiling of the old four-teacher label process. Together they quantify what the old supervision could ever have taught.

E2: forward-only forensics behind a 99% re-decode fidelity gate. It covers score-table decomposition, a whole-command versus trie-greedy decoding audit, a counterfactual sensitivity coefficient for posterior swaps against invariant edits, and hidden-state probes. This turns 'no sign the adapters read the posterior' into direct evidence.

E4: a CPU-only numerical learnability ladder (coarse N0 to the equivariant posterior net N2, 32 to 2,048 worlds, stress trajectories). It cheaply decides whether the state-to-action map is learnable at all.
Gates G1 to G8 become mandatory acceptance, including a closed-loop longest-run check. They replace the legality-only gate that let the November collapse pass.

Useful lemmas: trie-greedy picks the largest subtree mass; state-blind collapse under token-factorized logits; a Gibbs soft-target regret bound; with known per-action scores the exact expected gradient makes GRPO sampling unnecessary.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: The positive thesis is imitation of target risk in a class with a theorem-level ceiling. At best it shows 'the LLM matches the planner', which the literature notes grade as not novel (EVOLvE, DPT, Kriz et al.). The research question is reached only in E8 to E10, all marked 'should'.
Submission condition (4) (experimentalist task with transfer beyond the generator) is not addressed at all.

E3's 2x2x2 factorial needs 16 LLM runs, a new 800 to 1,200 line engine, and original-interface cells on 2 to 4k-token prompts, all for an in-sample attribution on 128 states. Its single-pass roster-order cells re-execute the old SFT recipe, close to the 'no old pipelines' rule.
Up to about 35 GPU slice-hours for E5 to E7 before any headroom evidence. The 20 GB slice runs only under gpu-testing with a 1-hour wall.
The E8 selection rule has a free branch ('if the hypothesized LLM contribution is semantic', policy-repair.md:331) that must be fixed now.
The power calculation for the counterfactual battery treats 300 states as independent although they come from 56 worlds. The E7(c) hidden-state linear head would not count as an LLM action policy.

strongest_ideas: The only proposal designed around condition (4): an independently authored simulator, billed time with a move-versus-replicate asymmetry, prose semantics, and an observable useful outcome (an operating point within pressure and flow specs at least current), decided by a shared chance-constrained rule so that arms differ only in the data they collect.
Device classes (fans, pumps, compressors, pressure sensing) are held out of training, so semantic transfer is tested out of distribution.
An LLM-independent numerical headroom audit (E1) runs before any LLM touches the task, with triviality checks and variance components.

E6 has a clean control set: anonymized semantics (L4), misleading text (L5), shuffled feedback (L6), graph withheld (L7), a frozen-embedding numerical student (N9), a compute-matched rollout (N5), and an argmax-of-prompt straddle rule (N7), with Holm over three primaries.
Theory on pool-replay unbiasedness for hardware and on CRN variance components.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: The headroom premise is weak: fan physics is monotone and smooth, so constrained knowledge-gradient planning likely solves the task. The two-round lever fallback (experimentalist-task.md:158) is a search for a configuration with headroom and must be registered and fully reported.

The semantic-transfer mechanism (a device library mapped to fan affinity laws) is speculative for a 0.6B model. It risks leakage from the library and recall of the public Causal Chambers documentation, and fresh paraphrases do not separate reading from recall.

Hardware calibration (E2) and a roughly 400 EUR hardware run (E9) are marked 'must' before any simulator evidence. They need a human sign-up and acceptance of terms (joint data ownership, marketing use of the name), a Python 3.11 environment, and a check of the call-home.

Missing comparators reviewers will demand: an LLM compiler or family-proposer feeding a numerical planner, and a robust model-averaging planner without text. The generic cubic-basis planner risks looking like a strawman.
No anatomy of the November collapse and only a minimal learnability check (500 steps), yet a full SFT plus GRPO stack of about 20 slice-hours is built from scratch.

One simulator family and one apparatus: the 128 'systems' are parameter perturbations of one simulator. pyCycle is unprototyped. Per-candidate probabilities in the prompt sit close to narration, so the LLM must clearly beat N7.

must_include: Week 0: correct the public record and register the decision tree before any new data. Correct the README and supersede the arXiv preprint first. Then hash a registration that maps each gate outcome to a claim and a venue and fixes every kill criterion and the class-admission rule. Justification: a new submission beside an uncorrected 70% claim from the same project is a credibility and integrity problem, and freezing the tree is the strongest defence against forking paths across a long, gated program.

Admit classes by a rule that is independent of the LLM. The headroom atlas covers at most three named candidates: structural knowledge given only in text (a sparse supergraph with absent edges or signs named in text); misspecification on the independently authored wind-tunnel simulator; and, only if human-written held-out text exists, the prose-objective class. The completed class is the negative control. Admission requires a ceiling gap over the strongest no-text controls (CRN target risk, rollout, law-aware planner, amortized no-text student), a residual the rule parser does not capture, a feasible n, and re-estimation of the gap on fresh calibration systems. Justification: this is the only defensible way to change benchmark under the no-favorable-replacement rule, and theory (equal-information ceiling, adaptivity of -0.7% +/- 1.7%) rules out an LLM win in the completed class.

Validate the measurement before any policy is scored. An in-process CRN planner must reproduce all 560 saved receipts. A truth-law (Rao-Blackwellized) evaluator is checked by A/A test size, planted-effect power, ERB-versus-realized unbiasedness, and synthetic policies of known capture, including a leakage policy. The primary endpoint is cost to a reliability target under a shared public stop rule, or fixed-budget truth-conditional error as the fallback, chosen by theory plus numerical-only calibration and never by first-crossing realized cost. Justification: Finding B showed the declared endpoint could not resolve policies, and only a validated instrument makes either a positive or a null result publishable.

Forward-only forensics of the saved base, SFT and final adapters on all 1,858 prompts, behind a 99% re-decode fidelity gate. Cover score tables, whole-command versus trie decoding, menu and identifier permutation, content-free prompts, and counterfactual posterior edits with world-clustered inference. Add probes, plus frozen capacity probes on 0.6B, 1.5B and 7B over compact renderings. Justification: this is cheap, needs no training and is decisive for the anatomy section of every paper branch, and the probe result decides in advance which escalation (on-policy RL or capacity) to use.

A learnability gate before any direct-policy work in a new class. First the CPU numerical ladder. Then one repaired recipe x 3 seeds: listwise planner targets, compact state, permuted single-token codes, whole-command argmax, shuffled minibatches, rank-16 all-linear LoRA. Add a label-permuted control, a numerical student on identical data, at most three knockouts (hard labels, raw envelope, trie decoding) and one predeclared escalation. Justification: every past LLM arm collapsed, condition (1) needs a reproducible policy, and the matched numerical student separates 'language cannot read the state' from 'the supervision was broken'.

A full equal-information comparator suite in the admitted class: CRN target risk and a rollout planner; a law-aware (empirical-Bayes) no-text planner; an amortized no-text student with a training-budget sweep (GO-CBED-style or equivariant); a rule parser plus planner; an LLM compiler plus numerical planner; a semantic-feature numerical student on frozen-LLM embeddings; the oracle-informed ceiling; a compute-matched planner; and the standing controls (frozen LLM, supervised LLM, numerical-ranker successor, target risk). Justification: these are the comparators the literature and the standing rules demand. Without the law-aware and compiler controls, a 'language' gain is confounded with learning the generator law, or dominated by a simpler hybrid.

Identification controls: text removed; misleading text with recovery delay; shuffled feedback, run only where the value of adaptivity is verified; state permutation; menu and identifier permutation; argmax-of-prompt whenever any derived statistic is in the prompt; and dose-response with a zero-dose placebo. Justification: these are the controls that separate contribution from narration, priors and identifier artifacts (Gupta et al., EVOLvE, Zheng et al.), and the dose-response shows the benefit tracks the information channel.

One preregistered fresh-system confirmation with methods, namespaces, endpoints and failure treatment frozen. Use CRN and at least 3 training seeds (5 preferred) for both the LLM and the numerical student. The evaluator is coded independently, a named analyst does the analysis, and arm labels are blinded. Holm over 2 to 3 primaries (against the strongest no-text control, and against the parser or compiler), TOST for the null branch, a leakage audit when capture exceeds the ceiling, and a failure ledger. Justification: submission conditions (2) and (5) require it, and single-seed results will be rejected.

Transfer of the frozen method to the wind-tunnel simulator family with an observable useful outcome (an operating point within spec at the lowest current) and counterfactual-law variants. Test superiority if the simulator was admitted and non-inferiority otherwise. The real Remote Lab runs only after a positive simulator result and Patrick's own sign-up and spend approval. Justification: condition (4) requires a concrete experimentalist task and transfer beyond the training generator, and this is the only available independently authored option with costs and semantics.
must_drop_or_change: Drop all LLM-superiority testing in the completed known-graph linear-Gaussian class. Use it only as the learnability arena and as a negative control on fresh systems. Justification: plan-once equals target risk, adaptivity is -0.7% +/- 1.7%, and the equal-information ceiling makes any win there chance.

policy-repair: demote 'Qwen recovers planner-quality decisions' from thesis to gate. Cut the E3 2x2x2 factorial to at most three knockouts inside the learnability gate, and drop the single-pass roster-order cells, which re-execute the old SFT recipe. Collapse E6 and E7 into one escalation chosen in advance by the forensic result. Do not count a hidden-state linear head as an LLM action policy, and fix the 'if semantic' branch of the E8 selection rule now. Justification: imitation of the teacher is not novel, and the factorial is the most expensive and least decisive item in the panel.

advantage-theory: add the frozen base LLM, the supervised LLM, a numerical-student control and at least 3 training seeds to E10, as the standing rules require. Restate the 'about 2% cap' as a bound pending the rollout, DP and law-aware references. Drop E9 or demote it to 'could', because it cannot show superiority. Cut the control suite to the required set, and re-estimate the selected headroom on fresh systems to avoid a winner's curse.

evaluation-statistics: remove the development LLM arms' positions from the endpoint-adoption criteria and report non-favorability only descriptively. Add natural-unit minimum important differences to the SD-unit class thresholds. Make hardware Stage B conditional on a positive Stage A. Justification: a measurement change must rest on criteria independent of LLM performance, and spend must be earned.

experimentalist-task: move hardware E2, E9 and E10 out of 'must' and make them conditional on a positive simulator result and a human sign-up. Register the whole lever family and report every configuration tried. Add the LLM-compiler and robust model-averaging planner controls. Demote pyCycle to 'could'. Justification: premature spend and terms acceptance, a forking-path risk, and missing comparators that reviewers will name.

paper-strategy: run the confirmation with at least 3 seeds instead of a single L*. Add a no-text law-aware planner and an amortized no-text student. Admit the prose-objective class K1 only if human-written held-out text exists, and otherwise lead with the structural-knowledge class. Add evaluator validation (A/A, planted effect, known capture). Drop the A6 and A7 knockouts that E2 already answers, and score the wind-tunnel transfer on an operating-point outcome, not NMSE.

Any arm that receives per-action planner scores or near-decision statistics (L2, L-adj, per-candidate probabilities) is a secondary or upper-bound control, never the primary arm, and is always reported with argmax-of-prompt. Justification: otherwise the LLM only narrates the optimizer, which the brief rules out.
No Remote Lab sign-up, hardware spend, 7B training or new compute ceilings before the gates that justify them. Each is an explicit ask to Patrick, released in stages.
missing_from_all: Text as the statistical unit. Claims that the LLM reads language generalize over texts, not systems. No proposal models system x text crossed random effects, or the effective n given by a few phrasing families or templates, in its power analysis or confirmation.

Winner's curse in class selection. Picking the cell with the largest headroom among many (about 60 in advantage-theory) inflates the gap. None re-estimates the selected class's headroom on fresh calibration systems before sizing the confirmation.

Counterfactual-law systems that separate reading from recall, where text and simulator consistently describe a modified exponent or a flipped sign. Anonymization, fresh paraphrases and misleading text show whether text is used and whether it harms, not whether it is read rather than recalled from pretraining (the Causal Chambers documentation is public).

A trained reasoning arm, or an explicit scope decision on reasoning tokens, for the transfer claim. Kriz et al. report that direct amortization without reasoning does not transfer robustly across domains, and Schmied et al. tie gains to chain of thought. Every proposal assumes no reasoning.

Amortization and total-cost accounting. None says how training simulation, privileged-teacher labels and synthetic responses count against the 'lower experimental cost' headline, as against savings per deployment.

A single hashed registration of the whole program decision tree (gate to claim to venue) with a global failure ledger across all development iterations and classes. Paper-strategy and evaluation-statistics each cover only part of this.

World-clustered inference for state-level analyses (counterfactual sensitivity, probes, gate statistics). States from the same world are not independent, and several power calculations treat them as if they were.

A predeclared non-inferiority (no-harm) fallback for the external transfer test if the wind-tunnel family has no admitted headroom. Condition (4) can then still be met with a correctly scoped claim, and transfer is not dropped.
judgment.recommended_spine: Week 0, with no compute: correct the README and supersede the arXiv preprint, then register a hashed program-level decision tree that fixes gate outcomes, claims, venues, every kill criterion and the class-admission rule, and obtain Patrick's rulings on which LLM role counts (direct policy, compiler or adjudicator), on whether a diagnostic paper is acceptable, and on venue. Weeks 1 to 3 run three tracks in parallel that need no new LLM training. (A) Measurement: an in-process common-random-number planner that must reproduce all 560 saved receipts, plus a truth-law Rao-Blackwellized evaluator validated by A/A size, planted effects and known-capture synthetic policies. (B) Forward-only forensics of the saved adapters behind a 99% fidelity gate, plus frozen capacity probes on 0.6B, 1.5B and 7B. (C) The value-gap decomposition of the completed screen with rollout and law-aware references, and the theory write-up (adaptivity and equal-information ceilings, endpoint efficiency, decoding lemma, label-noise bound). In weeks 2 to 5 a headroom atlas is scored only with numerical arms over at most three named classes: structural knowledge given only in text in a sparse supergraph, misspecification on the independently authored wind-tunnel simulator family, and a prose-objective class only if human-written text exists. The completed class serves as a negative control. Admission requires a ceiling gap over the strongest no-text controls, a rule-parser residual, a feasible n, and re-estimation on fresh calibration systems. In parallel a learnability gate runs: the CPU numerical ladder, then one repaired LLM recipe with 3 seeds, a label-permuted control, a numerical student on identical data, at most three knockouts, and one escalation chosen in advance from the forensic result. At Gate A, around week 6, if no class is admitted the program writes the theory, atlas, measurement and anatomy paper (ICML 2027 only if ready by about January 10, otherwise TMLR). If the LLM fails imitation while the numerical student passes, the direct-policy route closes and only the compiler role continues. In weeks 6 to 10, development in the admitted class uses privileged-teacher distillation plus DAgger against the full equal-information suite: CRN target risk, rollout, a law-aware planner, an amortized no-text student, a rule parser plus planner, an LLM compiler plus planner, a semantic-feature student, the oracle ceiling, the frozen and supervised LLMs, and a compute-matched planner. It also runs text-removed, misleading-text, shuffled-feedback, state-permutation and identifier controls, with dose strata that include a zero dose, and promotes one variant by a fixed rule on fresh validation shards in at most three iterations. Weeks 10 to 14 hold one preregistered fresh-system confirmation with everything frozen, CRN, at least 3 and preferably 5 seeds, independently coded evaluation, a named analyst, blinding, Holm over 2 to 3 primaries, TOST for the null branch, and a leakage audit. In weeks 12 to 16 the frozen method transfers to the wind-tunnel simulator family with an operating-point outcome and counterfactual-law variants. The test is superiority if the family was admitted and non-inferiority otherwise. The real Remote Lab is an optional demonstration, run only after a positive simulator result and Patrick's own sign-up and spend approval. The positive program realistically targets NeurIPS 2027 or TMLR, and ICML 2027 can carry only the diagnostic paper. Throughout, development runs on a light local in-process harness, with custody reserved for the confirmation, because operations rather than compute were the critical path in November.

strongest_ideas: Gate-ordered spine against real dates (Gate A about Dec 5, Gate B about Dec 23, ICML go/no-go about Jan 8, NeurIPS 2027 or TMLR target) with kill criteria K1 to K6 that can only narrow the claim, never add a benchmark.

E1 admission rule hashed before any LLM touches a new class, including the condition that a rule parser must leave at least 10% of the oracle gap on held-out paraphrase families. This is the honest test of whether a text-channel class needs an LLM.
Imitation ladder with knockouts and matched numerical students trained on identical data, with kill rules that separate a capacity failure from a supervision failure.
Transfer through the causalchamber wind-tunnel simulator with the knowingly misspecified linear learner (no new learner needed), and hardware strictly after simulator evidence.
Public-record correction (README, arXiv) before any new submission or talk.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: Gate A by Dec 5 needs, in about 2.5 weeks: K1 and K2 protocol modules, informed-prior learner support with new sealer and cost-curve versions, the CRN change (paired_episode.py:114-117), a truth-conditional evaluator, a rollout planner, the roster lift, three prose families and a parser. Optimistic.

E3 is costed at 4,000 states while its data paragraph gives about 9,600. At its own 5,000 tokens/s and 1.3x for rank 16, a run is about 1.0 to 1.3 slice-hours, which no longer fits a 1-hour gpu-testing job with checkpoint checks.
E4 7B LoRA training on a 36 GB Mac is unmeasured. E9 (delivery checkpoint diagnostics) needs a Duo-authenticated CURC retrieval and belongs to another paper.
Prose family D and the parser have no named author or effort budget. A weak parser or model-written prose inflates condition (b).

strongest_ideas: E4 numerical learnability ladder (N0 to N4, 32 to 2,048 worlds, planner relabels at zero environment cost). CPU only. It decides whether the planner's mapping is learnable from public state and sets the LLM's data volume and representation without any LLM output.

E1 high-precision CRN teacher with precision and rounding gates. Its cost basis checks out: 0.119 s per state at 16,384 draws (logged 499 s for 4,203 states, single process), and a scratch planner already reproduces 560/560 saved decisions.

Behavioural gate suite G1 to G8 as mandatory acceptance, with an in-training collapse abort. Interface repairs: permuted single-token codes, a compact planner-sufficient state, listwise soft targets, argmax over legal codes.
E8 class-selection rule fixed in advance with no LLM output. E6 DAgger only as a trigger.
Theory: trie-greedy versus whole-command argmax lemma, state-blind collapse lemma, label-information bound, exact single-step policy gradient, Gibbs soft-target regret bound.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: Weeks 1 to 5 and up to about 35 GPU-hours (E5 to E7) sit in the canonical class, where the proposal itself concedes the planner is the ceiling. The advantage track (E8 to E10) starts late and is underspecified: classes (i) to (iii) and the privileged teacher.

E3 (2x2x2 factorial on the 128 in-sample training states, 16 LLM and 24 CPU runs) is low evidence per GPU-hour. It needs the full new engine first, its own main risk is that every cell fails out of world, and its roster-order single-pass cells come close to the do-not-rerun rule.
E2's 12-edit donor-matched counterfactual battery (about 500 new lines, 16,400 forwards of 2,000 to 4,000 tokens at unmeasured MPS speed) is heavier than the evidence needs.
D4 (probes on development prompts) selects an E7 escalation arm. Method choices should rest on training-world probes only.

strongest_ideas: E1 endpoint non-favorability audit on saved data (under 1 CPU-hour). It is the cheapest way to make an endpoint change defensible under the no-favorable-replacement rule.
E2 harness validation before any policy is scored: A/A twin, planted-effect arm, CRN marginal checks, ERB unbiasedness, and variance components that size later studies.

Evaluator-side Rao-Blackwellized endpoint with stated validity conditions (T1), the threshold-averaging identity (T2), a TOST null branch, and the registered sizing rule S = max(48, min(150, formula)).
Contribution-isolation family (feedback-shuffled, state-permuted, compute-matched target risk, open-loop bound), plus blinded independent re-analysis with 10% re-execution.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: Not a full agenda. It has no class and no LLM recipe of its own and defers both to a method panel.

E5 allows 3 iterations x 3 recipes x 3 seeds, up to 27 LLM trainings plus students. E6 carries more than 15 arms with 5 seeds each for the LLM and the student, far beyond the 8-policy roster (paired_episode.py:94-95) and a heavy inference load.
E2 (1.5 to 3 weeks) is in effect the shared in-process bench that every proposal needs, but it is presented as a measurement step rather than budgeted as shared infrastructure.
ERB may need Monte Carlo in text-hint classes. E9 hardware adds human-gated spend before the simulator stage is proven.

strongest_ideas: Theory that makes class selection principled and independent of LLM performance: T1 (exact zero value of adaptivity in the design-only subclass), T4 (equal-information ceiling), T5 (gap decomposition), T6 (design value of side information), T7 (no power for the shuffled-feedback control where adaptivity is worthless).
E5 instrument calibration with synthetic policies of known capture, a leakage policy and a placebo. It validates the analysis before any LLM is scored and costs a few CPU-hours.
Dose-response design with zero-dose and placebo strata, and a ceiling audit: a gain above the computed ceiling triggers a leakage audit.
An explicit compiler-plus-planner (L3) versus policy (L1) contrast that surfaces the 'LLM as information channel' outcome honestly.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: E3's ten-control suite in 2 to 3 weeks is badly underestimated. It includes a GO-CBED-style transformer with a budget sweep (the public code needs download and install approval), a law-aware spike-and-slab planner, a reliability-aware text planner, a parser and a semantic-feature policy.

Its best class, C2 (sparse truth on a known supergraph), hits a verified constraint. The learner is built on the world graph (paired_episode.py:85, 177; cost_curves.py:119) and the assembler rejects a differing graph (scientific_campaign.py:158-159), so C2 needs a world-schema change or sealed-module changes. The 60-cell atlas, E8 and E9 add weeks.
Conflicts with standing rules. E10 omits the frozen LLM and supervised LLM controls. E1 rules (iii) and (iv) set successor class parameters from the private truth of the 24 development systems.
E7 leaves the LLM training recipe to an unspecified training workstream. It is about 13 weeks to E10 by its own estimate.

strongest_ideas: The only proposal that treats submission requirement 4 as a design problem: a concrete operating-point task with chamber-time costs on an independently authored simulator.

Hardware discipline: a shared fixed decision rule so arms differ only in interventions, pool-based replay without interpolation, a digital-twin dress rehearsal, and spend released only after simulator evidence.
Controls: a numerical student with frozen-LLM text embeddings (N9), anonymized and misleading-text arms, compute-matched rollout, and an argmax-of-prompt rule.
A numerical-only headroom audit before any LLM arm runs on a family, with namespaces frozen after the audit.
fatal_or_serious_flaws: E1 needs a basis-function Bayesian learner, which breaks the closed-form structural_moments recursion that target-risk planning relies on. It also needs state-dependent switching costs, CRN namespaces, a truth-conditional evaluator, raised roster and world limits, and new sealer and cost-curve versions. The 8 to 10 day estimate is optimistic by a factor of 2 or more.

E3 needs 16 device classes with 48 independently written descriptions. That is weeks of authoring and a large researcher-degrees-of-freedom surface, all before any evidence that the repaired training stack can produce a state-dependent policy.

The inferential chain is long: headroom on W, semantic information in the generator, learnability, in-distribution gates, zero-shot cross-family transfer, hardware. End-to-end probability is low. E5's 0.1 to 0.25 s step times at about 1,500 tokens are unmeasured and below the measured 0.6 s at about 3,000 tokens.

Many approvals and installs come early: Remote Lab sign-up with terms on joint data ownership and marketing use of the name, causalchamber 1.0.0rc1 in a Python 3.11 environment, and pyCycle/OpenMDAO with unverified Python 3.9 compatibility. The 9 to 10 week plan is realistically 16 to 20.

must_include: Experiment zero: one reviewed in-process bench, promoted from the scratch replays that already reproduce the saved artifacts (acelib.py to 1e-14, vtr.py 560/560 decisions to 1.1e-16). Contents: a callable-policy episode loop, a CRN planner beyond 256 draws, a rollout planner, the conjugate learner, a truth-conditional evaluator, and a leakage guard. Its acceptance test is fixed now: reproduce all 560 saved target-risk receipts, the saved CPU-arm public states and all 4,371 decision-state NMSEs. Justification: every proposal depends on it, and the existing harness cannot express it (episode.py:78 accepts only a ProcessPolicy, target_risk.py:102-103 caps draws at 256, paired_episode.py:94-95 caps the roster at 8, paired_episode.py:114-117 bans shared measurement namespaces).

judgment.recommended_spine: Phase 0 (November 12 to 19) uses no GPU. strongest_ideas: Rao-Blackwellized evaluation (ERB) with stated validity conditions, plus an explicit counterexample showing that the learner's posterior risk is biased and can be gamed when side information exists. This answers the circularity objection to model-based endpoints.

Harness validation before any new policy is scored: a CRN marginal check, the size of an A/A test, planted-effect power, ERB-versus-realized calibration, attribution agreement and stop-rule reliability.

A registered confirmation with blinded arm labels and all K = 5 trained seeds confirmed. It has a TOST null branch, no post hoc extension of n, no dropped systems, a failure ledger, an independent re-analysis and a 10% re-execution.
A fresh validation shard for each development iteration, with a hard cap of 3 iterations and the same tuning budget for every learned arm.

The T5 open-loop bound: the shuffled-feedback control can identify measurement use only where target risk beats plan-once. This stops an uninformative control from being read as evidence of measurement use.
Retiring the 24 development systems from all future decisions, plus a compute-matched target-risk control.

The '8 to 96 times fewer systems' figure was computed with the learner's posterior, which is biased in the 12 shifted systems. It must not be quoted until it is recomputed with ERB.

A 99% fidelity gate before any local forensic claim, and scoring over whole commands rather than greedy token decoding.

Parity with a numerical student trained on identical data, and a rule that a pass obtained only with per-action planner statistics in the prompt is narration and does not count.

Interventional attribution of the collapse on the original 128 training states: a factorial over labels, interface and exposure, with a numerical twin and a control whose labels are shuffled across states.
An explicit refusal to claim an advantage in the three-node known-graph class. The class changes only through a headroom rule that uses no LLM output.

Admit new classes by a rule that ignores LLM results, frozen and externally timestamped before any LLM is trained, prompted or scored in the class. Use numerical-only headroom against the strongest available references, show feasible n, include a zero-dose anchor, and declare a single primary class for the headline claim. Report every audited class, including failures and the completed three-node null, and allow at most two redesign rounds on LLM-independent criteria. Justification: this is what separates a theory-driven change of benchmark from a favorable replacement.

Write a declared-handicap table for each class before its headroom audit. It names what the uninformed planner lacks and the numerical control that removes each handicap: an oracle-informed planner; a hand-written parser plus planner, built to a stated effort standard by someone not developing the LLM; a learned non-LLM text model (bag-of-words); a numerical student on frozen-LLM embeddings; a GO-CBED-style amortized policy with a training-budget curve; a rollout planner; and a compute-matched planner. Every learned arm gets the same data and the same tuning budget, on validation data only. Justification: this is the standing rule that numerical controls receive the same information.

Make the confirmatory hypotheses co-primary. The LLM must beat both the strongest planner without the side information and the strongest numerical control that has the same information, and a full positive needs both. The confirmation must also contain: target risk; the numerical-student successor to the ranker; the frozen base LLM; the supervised-only LLM; text-removed, misleading-text, shuffled-feedback and state-permuted ablations; a control without language pretraining or using embeddings only; dose and placebo strata; and a leakage audit whenever a gain exceeds the computed ceiling. Justification: a win only over a planner that lacks the text shows that the text is valuable, which the audit already proves numerically. It does not show that the LLM contributes.

Validate the instrument on fresh calibration systems with numerical arms only, before any LLM is scored. This means a check of CRN marginals, an A/A test, planted-effect power, synthetic policies with known information capture, a leakage canary policy that reads the private truth, and a calibration of expected against realized error. The primary endpoint must be unbiased for an adaptive policy: either ERB (the conditional expectation given the data actually observed, under the generating law) or realized truth error with replicates. Design quality with redrawn noise stays secondary unless this validation passes.

Development discipline: training, validation, test and confirmation namespaces are disjoint and hashed. Use a fresh validation shard for each iteration, at most three iterations, and make every selection (recipe, lr, seed, escalation, DAgger round, model size) on validation data only. Score held-out test worlds once per frozen configuration. Record every attempt in a ledger and report the count in the paper.

Behavioural acceptance gates, fixed in advance, must pass before any rollout or outcome scoring: legality; no single action dominating; agreement beyond a coarse-feature baseline; held-out cross-entropy below a state-blind counter; sensitivity to posterior edits with invariance to menu order and identifiers; and stability across seeds. Justification: the November collapse passed a legality-only gate. Because the thresholds are calibrated knowing the November failures, the paper may say the gates would have caught it but may not call that a validation.

Fidelity-gated, forward-only forensics of the saved adapters must reproduce at least 99% of the saved decisions. Also check the base model's hash, because only the adapters are verified. Attribute the collapse interventionally with training-side factorial knockouts, using a numerical student on the same labels. Prompts from the development systems serve forensics only. Forensic outputs may change the method only through decision rules written before the forensics run, and any causal claim about the collapse needs interventional support.

Pre-register with an external timestamp before any confirmation system is generated. The registration fixes: hashes of methods and adapters; namespaces; endpoints; failure treatment (failures scored at the cap, no system replaced, aborted hardware episodes counted in the primary analysis); hypotheses; n; a TOST equivalence margin for a null; the seed policy (all trained seeds confirmed, with recipe-level and instance-level claims separated); and the hash of the analysis code. Arm labels stay blinded, and a human analyst re-analyses independently before results are released.

Controls against narration: no per-action planner statistics in the primary LLM input; a family of argmax-of-prompt rules; and a numerical student trained on exactly the prompt's features. Any adjudicator or re-ranker must deviate from argmax-of-prompt on a declared share of decisions, and those deviations must help on average. Hybrid and compiler roles are reported as narrowed claims that do not meet submission condition 1, unless the lead rules otherwise before any LLM result in the class.

Account for responses and compute: synthetic training-world responses, relabeling draws and training and inference compute are reported separately from deployment-time experimental cost. The 'lower experimental cost' claim refers only to deployment responses, and the numerical planners' zero training cost is shown alongside.

Kill rules only narrow the claim: if no class is admitted, the paper becomes theory, atlas and diagnostics; if imitation fails, it becomes the diagnostic paper; a failed confirmation is reported as such, with no replacement class. Throughout, an attempt ledger counts every LLM run, recipe, seed and class, and simulated training responses and compute are reported separately from deployment cost.
